# About this file

## What the deck answers

We measure how much economic growth, the size of government and health's share of the government budget accounted for the change in real government health spending per person in every country with data from 2000 to 2023. In Section 1 (slides 1 to 12), we report results for the world, income groups, World Bank regions and individual countries, then identify records to examine in detail. In Section 2 (slides 13 to 21), we consider budget years 2027 to 2029 and set out three amounts for every country: the minimum ask that holds health's share steady, an upper ask and the ceiling set by growth in the whole government budget. We list every country in two annexes (slides 22 to 35).

We rebuild every slide from the input data. Each slide has a heading, an explanation and a code chunk that computes its numbers, prints them in a table and draws its main figure. Our figures use the deck's numbers but not its layout. In the final chunk, we check every printed number against the output tables used to build the deck.

## The identity

We write government health spending per person as the product of three parts:

<p style="text-align:center"><b>government health spending per person = GDP per person &times; (government spending
&divide; GDP) &times; (government health spending &divide; government spending)</b></p>

We read the first part as the economy, the second as the size of government (general government expenditure as a share of GDP) and the third as health priority (domestic general government health expenditure as a share of general government expenditure). Natural logarithms turn the product into a sum, so the change in the logarithm of spending per person between two years splits exactly into the changes in the logarithms of its three parts. We calculate every change in this file as an average annual change in log points, 100 &times; ln(end value / start value) / number of years, which is close to a percentage change a year when changes are small. The identity means the three parts add up to the total in every country, period and group taken as a whole. Our split shows where a change came from in arithmetic; the identity does not explain why any part moved.

## The data

We use R data files (RDS) in `data/`. For each file, `data/README.md` records the source, retrieval date, size and sha256 of the CSV used to create it.

- We use `ghed_extract.rds`: World Health Organization Global Health Expenditure Database (GHED), 2025 update, retrieved
  28 May 2026. Seven series for every country and year: GDP per person and current health expenditure per person in
  current US\$, current health expenditure per person in constant 2023 US\$, general government expenditure as a share
  of GDP, domestic general government health expenditure as a share of general government expenditure and per person,
  and population.
- We use `countries.rds` and `group_labels.rds`: the 195 countries with their World Bank income group and region (2023
  classification, as published with the GHED 2025 update) and the group labels.
- We use `weo_currency_extract.rds`: IMF World Economic Outlook, October 2026, retrieved 23 October 2026. GDP in national
  currency at current and constant prices, general government expenditure as a share of GDP, GDP in US\$ and population,
  2024 to 2029. Used only by Section 2.
- We read `reference_outputs.rds` only in the final check; the file holds the report's own output tables.

## How to run it

1. Unzip the folder anywhere and open `global-decomposition-deck.Rmd` in RStudio. Knitting runs in the folder that
   holds the file, so the relative paths to `data/` and `fonts/` work without any change.
2. Install any missing package once: `install.packages(c("dplyr", "tidyr", "scales", "ggplot2", "knitr", "rmarkdown", "systemfonts", "ragg"))`.
3. Open `global-decomposition-deck.Rmd` and press Knit, or run `rmarkdown::render("global-decomposition-deck.Rmd")`.
   The whole file runs in about a minute and writes only the HTML file, next to the Rmd file.

Our figures use Open Sans. The six font files and their licence (SIL Open Font Licence 1.1) are in `fonts/` and are
registered at the start of the setup chunk, so nothing has to be installed on the computer.

# Setup and data

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
## Setup: packages, the Open Sans font shipped in fonts/, chunk options, colours, the
## plot theme and the way the slides print numbers. Every path in this file is
## relative to the folder that holds it.
# We use dplyr and tidyr for the tables, scales for printing numbers and ggplot2 for the figures
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

# We register the Open Sans files shipped in fonts/, so the figures look the same on any computer
font_styles <- c("Regular", "Bold", "Italic", "BoldItalic", "SemiBold", "SemiBoldItalic")
font_files <- file.path("fonts", paste0("OpenSans-", font_styles, ".ttf"))
names(font_files) <- font_styles
if (!"Open Sans" %in% systemfonts::registry_fonts()$family) {
  registered <- tryCatch(
    {
      systemfonts::register_font(
        "Open Sans",
        plain = font_files[["Regular"]],
        bold = font_files[["Bold"]],
        italic = font_files[["Italic"]],
        bolditalic = font_files[["BoldItalic"]]
      )
      TRUE
    },
    error = function(e) FALSE
  )
  # a computer with Open Sans installed refuses the registration; we then side-load the files, and
  # systemfonts searches side-loaded files first, so the figures still use the files in fonts/
  if (!registered) systemfonts::add_fonts(unname(font_files))
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  dev = "ragg_png", dpi = 150, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.2, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE
)
FONT <- "Open Sans"

# World Bank colours used by the deck
WB <- c(
  blue = "#0071bc", navy = "#002244", rust = "#b5452c", grey = "#9aa3ad", grey2 = "#8f99a3",
  light = "#7fc4ea", sky = "#5fb3e4", slate = "#5b6470", tint = "#dcebf6", rosy = "#f2c9bd",
  pale = "#c9d0d6"
)
PART_LABEL <- c(
  econ = "Economy", budget = "Size of government", priority = "Health priority", total = "Total"
)
PART_FILL <- c(
  Economy = "#8f99a3", "Size of government" = "#7fc4ea", "Health priority" = "#0071bc",
  Total = "#002244"
)

# One theme for every figure: Open Sans, explicit black x and y
# axis lines, light major gridlines only
figure_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11, base_family = FONT) +
  theme(
    axis.line = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5),
    axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(colour = "black"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#e6e9ec", linewidth = 0.3),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = WB[["navy"]]),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "#3a434d"),
    plot.caption = element_text(colour = WB[["slate"]], hjust = 0),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0)
  )
theme_set(figure_theme)
# we write the numbers and labels on the charts in Open Sans as well
update_geom_defaults("text", list(family = FONT))

# How the slides print numbers. The deck rounds each number once and the slide only prints it, so we
# round and print in one step with the labelling functions of scales.
signed <- scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1, style_positive = "plus") # +1.2, -0.4, 0.0
one_decimal <- scales::label_comma(accuracy = 0.1) # 1,234.5
share_pct <- scales::label_percent(accuracy = 0.1, scale = 1, big.mark = ",") # 12.3% from per cent
signed_pct <- scales::label_percent(
  accuracy = 0.1, scale = 1, big.mark = ",", style_positive = "plus"
) # +12.3%
whole_pct <- scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1, scale = 1, big.mark = ",") # 1,234%

# The slides print dollars whole from US$100 and with one decimal below. We keep this small function
# because no scales labeller changes its accuracy with the size of the number.
dollars <- function(x, prefix = "US$") {
  whole <- scales::comma(x, accuracy = 1, prefix = prefix)
  with_decimal <- scales::comma(x, accuracy = 0.1, prefix = prefix)
  ifelse(abs(x) >= 100, whole, with_decimal)
}

# knitr::kable() prints one table, and each slide has a few, so this function prints a slide's list
# of tables. We right-align the columns that hold only numbers, as the slides do.
show_tables <- function(tables) {
  for (caption in names(tables)) {
    table <- tables[[caption]]
    align <- rep("l", ncol(table))
    for (j in seq_along(table)[-1]) {
      column <- as.character(table[[j]])
      numbers_only <- grepl("^[-+0-9.,%/ US$]*$", column) | column %in% c("-", "Not available")
      if (all(numbers_only)) align[j] <- "r"
    }
    cat("\n\n")
    print(knitr::kable(table, caption = caption, row.names = FALSE, align = align))
    cat("\n\n")
  }
}

# The bar chart of slides 3, 4, 10 and 11. We keep it as a function because four slides draw it and
# ggplot2 has no single geom for it: one bar per row of `parts`, the three parts stacked (the
# economy nearest zero) and the total as a diamond, with the total printed in a column right of the
# bars. `parts` has the columns econ, budget, priority and total, the bar labels in `label_col` and,
# if `facet` is given, the panel of each bar.
plot_parts <- function(parts, label_col, xlab = "Average annual change, log points", facet = NULL) {
  # we keep the first row at the top of the chart
  bar_labels <- parts[[label_col]]
  parts$row <- factor(bar_labels, levels = rev(unique(bar_labels)))
  parts$panel <- if (is.null(facet)) "" else parts[[facet]]

  # one bar segment per row and part
  part_names <- PART_LABEL[c("econ", "budget", "priority")]
  bars <- parts |>
    select(row, panel, econ, budget, priority) |>
    pivot_longer(c(econ, budget, priority), names_to = "part", values_to = "value") |>
    mutate(part = factor(PART_LABEL[part], levels = part_names))

  # we print the totals just right of the bar that reaches furthest
  reach_right <- pmax(parts$econ, 0) + pmax(parts$budget, 0) + pmax(parts$priority, 0)
  reach_left <- pmin(parts$econ, 0) + pmin(parts$budget, 0) + pmin(parts$priority, 0)
  chart_width <- max(reach_right, parts$total, 0) - min(reach_left, parts$total, 0)
  parts$label_x <- max(reach_right, parts$total) + 0.06 * chart_width

  chart <- ggplot(bars, aes(x = value, y = row)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = part), width = 0.7, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(
      data = parts, aes(x = total, y = row),
      shape = 23, size = 2.8, fill = WB[["navy"]], colour = "white"
    ) +
    geom_text(
      data = parts, aes(x = label_x, y = row, label = signed(total)),
      hjust = 0, size = 3.2, colour = WB[["navy"]], fontface = "bold"
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.12))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = PART_FILL) +
    labs(
      x = xlab, y = NULL,
      caption = "Bars: the three parts. Diamond and right-hand number: the total."
    )
  if (!is.null(facet)) {
    chart <- chart + facet_grid(panel ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y")
  }
  chart
}
```

```{r read-data}
## Read the inputs: four RDS files converted one to one from the report's
## CSV inputs (same columns, same types).
# WHO GHED 2025 update, one row per country, year and series
ghed_long <- readRDS("data/ghed_extract.rds")
# the 195 countries with their World Bank income group and region
countries <- readRDS("data/countries.rds")
# labels and member counts of the income groups and regions
group_labels <- readRDS("data/group_labels.rds")
# IMF WEO October 2026, 2024 to 2029, one row per country, year and series (Section 2 only)
weo_long <- readRDS("data/weo_currency_extract.rds")
stopifnot(nrow(ghed_long) > 0, nrow(countries) == 195)
data.frame(
  file = c("ghed_extract", "countries", "group_labels", "weo_currency_extract"),
  rows = c(nrow(ghed_long), nrow(countries), nrow(group_labels), nrow(weo_long)),
  columns = c(ncol(ghed_long), ncol(countries), ncol(group_labels), ncol(weo_long))
)
```

# Cleaning

We start with the GHED extract, which is already tidy, so the cleaning is short. The next chunk records each decision that affects a number and the reason for that decision.

- **Study period and windows.** We use 2000 to 2023 for the trend and fixed periods. Each country gets a
  latest window: ten years ending at the latest year, up to 2024, in which all three parts are published, starting at
  the earliest year from ten years back that also has all parts, and never shorter than five years. The rule is the
  one the country profile slide uses, so the numbers agree with the country decks. Seven countries have 2024 data in
  GHED, which is released in stages, so the windows of those seven countries run 2014-2024.
- **Fixed periods.** We use 2000-2010, 2010-2019 and 2019-2023 to compare the same years in every country: the 2000s, the
  decade up to the pandemic, and the pandemic years with their partial reversal. Exact end years are used, with no
  substitution of a nearby year.
- **Data flags.** We apply four rules inside each country's window to mark series that make a rate hard to read. A break
  (B) is a budget share or health share that doubles or halves from one year to the next, which is where
  reclassifications in the accounts usually sit. A shock (S) is real GDP per person rising by more than 25% or falling
  by more than 20% in one year: war, conversion artefacts after high inflation, the 2020 collapse in tourism, oil booms.
  An extreme end (E) is a share in the first or last year of the window more than twice or less than half its own
  median over the window, which makes an endpoint rate unrepresentative. A level flag (L) is government spending above
  100% of GDP or government health spending below US\$1 per person at either end. Flagged countries stay in every
  median and aggregate but are left out of the instructive examples and listed apart among the warning cases.
- **Real terms.** We use GHED's current health expenditure per person in current US\$ and constant 2023 US\$. We take the ratio of the two as GHED's own conversion factor for each country and year, then apply the factor to GDP per person. The two shares are ratios and need no conversion. One conversion for everything keeps the identity exact in constant prices, and we use the same conversion as the country profile slide. The factor mixes domestic prices and exchange rates, one of the limits we discuss on slide 12.
- **Which country-years enter.** We keep a country-year only when the conversion factor, GDP per person and both shares
  are published and above zero, since every part enters as a logarithm.

```{r clean}
## Cleaning: from the long GHED extract to one row per country and year with the
## identity's three parts in real terms.
# ---- 0. Decisions that shape the numbers ---------------------------------------------------------
YEAR_MIN <- 2000 # first year of the study period
YEAR_MAX <- 2023 # last year of the study period (fixed periods, trends)
WINDOW_MAX_YEAR <- 2024 # latest year a window may end in: GHED's last, as on the country slide
WINDOW <- 10 # window of ten years ending at the latest year with all parts
MIN_SPAN <- 5 # shortest window accepted
PERIODS <- tibble(
  period = c("P1", "P2", "P3"),
  y0 = c(2000, 2010, 2019),
  y1 = c(2010, 2019, 2023)
)
FLAG_RATIO_STEP <- log(2) # B, break: a budget share or the health share doubles or halves in a year
FLAG_GDP_STEP <- log(1.25) # S, shock: real GDP per person up more than 25% or down more than 20%
FLAG_END <- log(2) # E, extreme end: a share at an end over twice or under half its window median
FLAG_PIE_MAX <- 100 # L, level: government spending above 100% of GDP at either end, or
FLAG_GHE_MIN <- 1 #    government health spending below US$1 per person (2023 US$) at either end

# ---- 1. One row per country and year, one column per series --------------------------------------
panel <- ghed_long |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  select(iso3, year, indicator, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = indicator, values_from = value) |>
  arrange(iso3, year)

# ---- 2. Real terms: GHED's constant-2023-US$ conversion factor k, applied to GDP per person ------
# k is the ratio of GHED's two health spending series where both are published and above zero.
# Every part enters as a logarithm, so we keep a country-year only when k, GDP per person and both
# shares are published and above zero.
panel <- panel |>
  mutate(
    k = if_else(che_usd2023_pc > 0 & che_pc_usd > 0, che_usd2023_pc / che_pc_usd, NA),
    ok = !is.na(k) & !is.na(gdp_pc_usd) & gdp_pc_usd > 0 & !is.na(gge_gdp) & gge_gdp > 0 &
      !is.na(gghed_gge) & gghed_gge > 0,
    gdp_real = if_else(ok, gdp_pc_usd * k, NA), # real GDP per person, 2023 US$
    pie = if_else(ok, gge_gdp, NA), # government spending, % of GDP
    slice = if_else(ok, gghed_gge, NA), # health, % of government spending
    ghe_real = gdp_real * pie / 100 * slice / 100, # government health spending per person
    # we also rebuild spending in current US$ and compare it with GHED's own published series
    ghe_cur = if_else(ok, gdp_pc_usd * pie / 100 * slice / 100, NA),
    ident_gap_pct = 100 * (ghe_cur / gghed_pc_usd - 1)
  )

# ---- 3. Country attributes ----------------------------------------------------------------------
panel <- panel |>
  left_join(select(countries, iso3, name, income_group, wb_region), by = "iso3") |>
  arrange(iso3, year)
largest_gap <- max(abs(panel$ident_gap_pct), na.rm = TRUE)
data.frame(
  `country-years` = nrow(panel),
  `with all parts` = sum(panel$ok),
  countries = length(unique(panel$iso3)),
  `largest gap to GHED's own per person series, %` = signif(largest_gap, 2),
  check.names = FALSE
)
```

We use the last column above to compare the product of the three parts in current US\$ with GHED's own series for government
health spending per person. The largest gap is a tiny fraction of one per cent, a rounding difference in the published
values, so the identity holds in the data and not only on paper.

# The decomposition engine

## Country windows, periods and flags

In the next chunk, we do the country-level work. For each country the chunk picks the latest window, splits the change over the
window into the three parts, splits the window into two halves at its middle year (used by the instructive examples),
applies the four data flags and names the pattern of change. The pattern rule is plain arithmetic: a country is
"declining" if spending per person fell over the window, and otherwise named after the largest of the three parts
(economy-led, budget-led or priority-led). "Health lost priority" means the economy part was positive while the health
priority part was negative. The same split is then made for each of the three fixed periods, for every country with all
parts at both ends of the period.

We treat the instructive examples and warning cases as rules, not rankings. An instructive example grew in the top quarter
of its income group, got at least half of the growth from the size of government and health priority together, grew in
both halves of its window and carries no data flag. A warning case either spent less per person at the end of its
window, or saw health priority take away at least half of what the economy added.

```{r engine-countries}
## Country level: each country's latest window, its decomposition, halves, flags, pattern, example
## and warning status; then the same decomposition for the three fixed periods.
# we work only with the country-years that have all three parts
years_with_parts <- panel |>
  filter(ok) |>
  arrange(iso3, year)

# labels of the income groups and regions, in the order the deck uses
group_label <- setNames(group_labels$label, paste(group_labels$grouping, group_labels$key))
inc_levels <- c("low", "lower_middle", "upper_middle", "high")
reg_levels <- c(
  "East Asia & Pacific", "Europe & Central Asia", "Latin America & Caribbean",
  "Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan", "North America", "South Asia",
  "Sub-Saharan Africa", "not_classified"
)

# Every window a country could have: an end year up to 2024 and a start year with all parts, at most
# ten and at least five years earlier
start_years <- select(years_with_parts, iso3, y0 = year)
possible_windows <- years_with_parts |>
  filter(year <= WINDOW_MAX_YEAR) |>
  select(iso3, y1 = year) |>
  inner_join(start_years, by = "iso3", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  filter(y0 >= YEAR_MIN, y0 >= y1 - WINDOW, y0 <= y1 - MIN_SPAN)

# we take the latest end year, and for it the earliest start year
window_years <- possible_windows |>
  group_by(iso3) |>
  filter(y1 == max(y1)) |>
  summarise(y0 = min(y0), y1 = first(y1))

# the four series at the start, the middle and the end of a window, ready to join on
start_values <- years_with_parts |>
  select(iso3, y0 = year, ghe0 = ghe_real, gdp0 = gdp_real, pie0 = pie, slice0 = slice)
end_values <- years_with_parts |>
  select(iso3, y1 = year, ghe1 = ghe_real, gdp1 = gdp_real, pie1 = pie, slice1 = slice)
middle_values <- years_with_parts |>
  select(iso3, mid = year, ghe_mid = ghe_real)

# The change over the window split into the three parts, in log points a year; the parts add up to
# the total. We also split the window at its middle year (rounded half up, as the slide rounds it).
windows <- window_years |>
  left_join(start_values, by = c("iso3", "y0")) |>
  left_join(end_values, by = c("iso3", "y1")) |>
  mutate(
    span = y1 - y0,
    mid = y0 + floor(span / 2 + 0.5),
    econ = 100 * log(gdp1 / gdp0) / span,
    budget = 100 * log(pie1 / pie0) / span,
    priority = 100 * log(slice1 / slice0) / span,
    total = 100 * log(ghe1 / ghe0) / span
  ) |>
  left_join(middle_values, by = c("iso3", "mid")) |>
  mutate(
    half1 = 100 * log(ghe_mid / ghe0) / (mid - y0),
    half2 = 100 * log(ghe1 / ghe_mid) / (y1 - mid)
  )

# The four data flags inside each window. The year-on-year rules B and S compare consecutive years
# only; the rules E and L look at the first and the last year.
window_flags <- years_with_parts |>
  inner_join(window_years, by = "iso3") |>
  filter(year >= y0, year <= y1) |>
  group_by(iso3) |>
  arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    log_pie = log(pie),
    log_slice = log(slice),
    log_gdp = log(gdp_real),
    consecutive = year - lag(year) == 1,
    pie_step = abs(log_pie - lag(log_pie)),
    slice_step = abs(log_slice - lag(log_slice)),
    gdp_step = abs(log_gdp - lag(log_gdp)),
    big_step = pie_step > FLAG_RATIO_STEP | slice_step > FLAG_RATIO_STEP,
    is_end = year == y0 | year == y1,
    pie_median = median(pie),
    slice_median = median(slice),
    pie_off_median = abs(log(pie / pie_median)),
    slice_off_median = abs(log(slice / slice_median))
  ) |>
  summarise(
    flag_B = any(consecutive & big_step, na.rm = TRUE),
    flag_S = any(consecutive & gdp_step > FLAG_GDP_STEP, na.rm = TRUE),
    flag_E = any(is_end & (pie_off_median > FLAG_END | slice_off_median > FLAG_END)),
    flag_L = any(is_end & (pie > FLAG_PIE_MAX | ghe_real < FLAG_GHE_MIN)),
    n_years_in_window = n()
  )

# One row per country, with or without a window. The pattern is plain arithmetic: declining if the
# total fell, otherwise named after the largest of the three parts (the first one on a tie).
country_windows <- countries |>
  select(iso3, name, income_group, wb_region) |>
  left_join(windows, by = "iso3") |>
  left_join(window_flags, by = "iso3") |>
  arrange(iso3) |>
  mutate(
    has_window = !is.na(total),
    closure = econ + budget + priority - total, # the identity check, about zero
    flag_letters = paste0(
      if_else(flag_B, "B ", ""),
      if_else(flag_S, "S ", ""),
      if_else(flag_E, "E ", ""),
      if_else(flag_L, "L", "")
    ),
    flag = if_else(has_window, trimws(flag_letters), NA),
    flagged = has_window & nzchar(flag),
    note_2024 = has_window & y1 == 2024,
    note_short = has_window & span < WINDOW,
    pattern = case_when(
      total < 0 ~ "Declining",
      econ >= budget & econ >= priority ~ "Economy-led",
      budget >= priority ~ "Budget-led",
      budget < priority ~ "Priority-led"
    ),
    lost_priority = has_window & econ > 0 & priority < 0
  ) |>
  select(-flag_letters)

# Instructive examples and warning cases are rules applied within each income group
country_windows <- country_windows |>
  group_by(income_group) |>
  mutate(top_quarter = has_window & total >= quantile(total[has_window], 0.75, names = FALSE)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    example = has_window & top_quarter & total > 0 & (budget + priority) >= 0.5 * total &
      !is.na(half1) & half1 > 0 & half2 > 0 & !flagged,
    warning_rule = has_window & (total < 0 | (econ > 0 & priority <= -0.5 * econ)),
    warning = warning_rule & !flagged,
    inc_lab = unname(group_label[paste("income", income_group)]),
    reg_lab = unname(group_label[paste("wb_region", wb_region)])
  )

# The fixed periods: one decomposition per country and period, for every country with all parts at
# both ends of the period (we use the same pattern rule as above)
country_periods <- years_with_parts |>
  select(
    iso3, income_group, wb_region,
    y0 = year, gdp0 = gdp_real, pie0 = pie, slice0 = slice, ghe0 = ghe_real
  ) |>
  inner_join(PERIODS, by = "y0") |>
  inner_join(end_values, by = c("iso3", "y1")) |>
  arrange(period, iso3) |>
  mutate(
    econ = 100 * log(gdp1 / gdp0) / (y1 - y0),
    budget = 100 * log(pie1 / pie0) / (y1 - y0),
    priority = 100 * log(slice1 / slice0) / (y1 - y0),
    total = 100 * log(ghe1 / ghe0) / (y1 - y0),
    pattern = case_when(
      total < 0 ~ "Declining",
      econ >= budget & econ >= priority ~ "Economy-led",
      budget >= priority ~ "Budget-led",
      budget < priority ~ "Priority-led"
    ),
    lost_priority = econ > 0 & priority < 0
  ) |>
  select(
    period, y0, y1, iso3, income_group, wb_region, econ, budget, priority, total, pattern,
    lost_priority
  )
data.frame(
  countries = nrow(country_windows),
  `with a window` = sum(country_windows$has_window),
  `largest closure error` = max(abs(country_windows$closure), na.rm = TRUE),
  flagged = sum(country_windows$flagged),
  examples = sum(country_windows$example),
  `warning cases without a flag` = sum(country_windows$warning),
  check.names = FALSE
)
```

## Groups: the median country and the group as a whole

We use two summaries for a group in the deck. The **median country** is the median of countries' rates, calculated separately for each part; the three part medians therefore need not add up to the median total. The **group as a whole** sums real GDP (GDP per person times population), government spending and government health spending, then divides each sum by the summed population. The identity also holds for these sums, so the parts add up exactly. Because an aggregate needs the same years for every member, the latest-window aggregate uses 2013 and 2023, the window used by most countries, while the latest-window median uses each country's own window. Groups with fewer than eight countries are described but not compared.

For 2000 to 2023, we build trend series of medians and quartiles for all countries with data in each year and for the balanced panel with all parts throughout. We also track health's spending share around the pandemic (2019, 2021 and 2023 for the same countries), count patterns and calculate each low-income country's contribution to group spending.

```{r engine-groups}
## Group level: medians and aggregates by period and latest window, sensitivity without
## flagged countries, trends, the pandemic trajectories, pattern counts and each country's
## share of its income group's change.

# the thirteen groups (world, four income groups, eight regions) and the countries in each
groups <- bind_rows(
  tibble(grouping = "world", key = "world", label = "World", N = nrow(countries)),
  select(group_labels, grouping, key, label, N = n_members)
) |>
  arrange(match(key, c("world", inc_levels, reg_levels)))
membership <- bind_rows(
  transmute(countries, grouping = "world", key = "world", iso3),
  transmute(countries, grouping = "income", key = income_group, iso3),
  transmute(countries, grouping = "wb_region", key = wb_region, iso3)
)
flagged_countries <- country_windows$iso3[country_windows$flagged]

# The median country: each part's median taken separately over the group's countries, for the three
# periods and the latest window ("W"), with all countries and without the flagged ones
country_rates <- bind_rows(
  select(country_periods, period, iso3, econ, budget, priority, total),
  country_windows |>
    filter(has_window) |>
    transmute(period = "W", iso3, econ, budget, priority, total)
)
rates_for_medians <- bind_rows(
  mutate(country_rates, sample = "all"),
  country_rates |>
    filter(period == "W", !iso3 %in% flagged_countries) |>
    mutate(sample = "without flagged")
)
group_medians <- rates_for_medians |>
  inner_join(membership, by = "iso3", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  group_by(sample, grouping, key, period) |>
  summarise(
    med_econ = median(econ),
    med_budget = median(budget),
    med_priority = median(priority),
    med_total = median(total),
    n_med = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# A group as a whole: real GDP, government spending and government health spending summed over
# the members, then divided by the summed population (and by each other for the two shares),
# so the identity holds for the sums. A whole needs the same two years for every member, so
# the latest window uses 2013 and 2023.
whole_years <- tibble(
  period = c("P1", "P2", "P3", "W"),
  y0 = c(2000, 2010, 2019, 2013),
  y1 = c(2010, 2019, 2023, 2023)
)
money <- years_with_parts |>
  filter(!is.na(pop)) |>
  mutate(gdp = gdp_real * pop, gge = gdp * pie / 100, ghe = gge * slice / 100) |>
  select(iso3, year, pop, gdp, gge, ghe)
money_start <- rename(money, y0 = year, pop0 = pop, gdp0 = gdp, gge0 = gge, ghe0 = ghe)
money_end <- rename(money, y1 = year, pop1 = pop, gdp1 = gdp, gge1 = gge, ghe1 = ghe)

# every member with all parts and population at both ends of each period
members_both_ends <- membership |>
  cross_join(whole_years) |>
  inner_join(money_start, by = c("iso3", "y0")) |>
  inner_join(money_end, by = c("iso3", "y1")) |>
  arrange(iso3)
members_for_wholes <- bind_rows(
  mutate(members_both_ends, sample = "all"),
  members_both_ends |>
    filter(period == "W", !iso3 %in% flagged_countries) |>
    mutate(sample = "without flagged")
)
group_wholes <- members_for_wholes |>
  group_by(sample, grouping, key, period, y0, y1) |>
  summarise(
    gdp_start = sum(gdp0) / sum(pop0),
    pie_start = 100 * sum(gge0) / sum(gdp0),
    slice_start = 100 * sum(ghe0) / sum(gge0),
    ghe_start = sum(ghe0) / sum(pop0),
    gdp_end = sum(gdp1) / sum(pop1),
    pie_end = 100 * sum(gge1) / sum(gdp1),
    slice_end = 100 * sum(ghe1) / sum(gge1),
    ghe_end = sum(ghe1) / sum(pop1),
    n_agg = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    agg_econ = 100 * log(gdp_end / gdp_start) / (y1 - y0),
    agg_budget = 100 * log(pie_end / pie_start) / (y1 - y0),
    agg_priority = 100 * log(slice_end / slice_start) / (y1 - y0),
    agg_total = 100 * log(ghe_end / ghe_start) / (y1 - y0)
  ) |>
  select(sample, grouping, key, period, agg_econ, agg_budget, agg_priority, agg_total, n_agg)

# Each group in each fixed period and over the latest window, with every country
medians_all <- group_medians |>
  filter(sample == "all") |>
  select(-sample)
wholes_all <- group_wholes |>
  filter(sample == "all") |>
  select(-sample)
group_summary <- groups |>
  cross_join(whole_years) |>
  left_join(medians_all, by = c("grouping", "key", "period")) |>
  left_join(wholes_all, by = c("grouping", "key", "period")) |>
  mutate(
    years = if_else(
      period == "W", "Latest window (aggregate 2013 to 2023)", paste0(y0, " to ", y1)
    ),
    n_med = coalesce(n_med, 0L),
    n_agg = coalesce(n_agg, 0L),
    status = if_else(n_med >= 8, "Carries a comparison",
      "Fewer than 8 countries: described, not compared"
    ),
    agg_closure = agg_econ + agg_budget + agg_priority - agg_total
  ) |>
  select(
    grouping, key, label, N, period, years, med_econ, med_budget, med_priority, med_total,
    n_med, agg_econ, agg_budget, agg_priority, agg_total, n_agg, status, agg_closure
  )

# Sensitivity: the latest-window medians and the 2013-2023 wholes without the flagged countries
medians_without_flagged <- groups |>
  left_join(
    filter(group_medians, sample == "without flagged"),
    by = c("grouping", "key")
  ) |>
  mutate(n_med = coalesce(n_med, 0L)) |>
  select(grouping, key, label, med_econ, med_budget, med_priority, med_total, n_med)
wholes_without_flagged <- groups |>
  left_join(
    filter(group_wholes, sample == "without flagged"),
    by = c("grouping", "key")
  ) |>
  mutate(n_agg = coalesce(n_agg, 0L)) |>
  select(grouping, key, label, agg_econ, agg_budget, agg_priority, agg_total, n_agg)

# Each country's government health spending in US$ million (2023 prices) in 2013 and 2023, and its
# share of its income group's change (population is in thousands)
spending_2013 <- years_with_parts |>
  filter(year == 2013, !is.na(pop)) |>
  transmute(iso3, ghe0_musd = ghe_real * pop / 1000, pop0_m = pop / 1000)
spending_2023 <- years_with_parts |>
  filter(year == 2023, !is.na(pop)) |>
  transmute(iso3, ghe1_musd = ghe_real * pop / 1000, pop1_m = pop / 1000)
contributions <- countries |>
  select(income_group, iso3, name) |>
  inner_join(spending_2013, by = "iso3") |>
  inner_join(spending_2023, by = "iso3") |>
  arrange(match(income_group, inc_levels), iso3) |>
  group_by(income_group) |>
  mutate(
    share_of_group_change_pct = 100 * (ghe1_musd - ghe0_musd) / sum(ghe1_musd - ghe0_musd),
    change_pct_of_group_2013 = 100 * (ghe1_musd - ghe0_musd) / sum(ghe0_musd)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Trends 2000 to 2023: medians and quartiles over all countries with data each year, and the
# balanced panel (all parts in every year) as a whole and as medians
study_years <- years_with_parts |>
  filter(year >= YEAR_MIN, year <= YEAR_MAX)
years_per_country <- count(study_years, iso3)
balanced <- years_per_country$iso3[years_per_country$n == length(YEAR_MIN:YEAR_MAX)]
balanced <- intersect(balanced, years_with_parts$iso3[!is.na(years_with_parts$pop)])
trend_members <- study_years |>
  inner_join(membership, by = "iso3", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  arrange(iso3)
trend_all_countries <- trend_members |>
  group_by(grouping, key, year) |>
  summarise(
    med_ghe = median(ghe_real),
    p25_ghe = quantile(ghe_real, 0.25, names = FALSE),
    p75_ghe = quantile(ghe_real, 0.75, names = FALSE),
    n = n(),
    med_slice = median(slice),
    p25_slice = quantile(slice, 0.25, names = FALSE),
    p75_slice = quantile(slice, 0.75, names = FALSE),
    med_pie = median(pie),
    med_gdp = median(gdp_real),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
trend_balanced <- trend_members |>
  filter(iso3 %in% balanced, !is.na(pop)) |>
  mutate(gdp = gdp_real * pop, gge = gdp * pie / 100, ghe = gge * slice / 100) |>
  group_by(grouping, key, year) |>
  summarise(
    agg_ghe = sum(ghe) / sum(pop),
    agg_slice = 100 * sum(ghe) / sum(gge),
    agg_pie = 100 * sum(gge) / sum(gdp),
    agg_gdp = sum(gdp) / sum(pop),
    n_bal = n(),
    med_ghe_bal = median(ghe_real),
    p25_ghe_bal = quantile(ghe_real, 0.25, names = FALSE),
    p75_ghe_bal = quantile(ghe_real, 0.75, names = FALSE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
trends <- groups |>
  select(grouping, key, label) |>
  cross_join(tibble(year = YEAR_MIN:YEAR_MAX)) |>
  left_join(trend_all_countries, by = c("grouping", "key", "year")) |>
  left_join(trend_balanced, by = c("grouping", "key", "year")) |>
  mutate(n = coalesce(n, 0L), n_bal = coalesce(n_bal, 0L))

# Health's share around the pandemic: 2019, 2021 and 2023 for the same countries, and five paths
share_2021 <- years_with_parts |>
  filter(year == 2021) |>
  select(iso3, s21 = slice)
share_2023 <- years_with_parts |>
  filter(year == 2023) |>
  select(iso3, s23 = slice)
pandemic_countries <- years_with_parts |>
  filter(year == 2019) |>
  select(iso3, s19 = slice, income_group, wb_region) |>
  left_join(share_2021, by = "iso3") |>
  left_join(share_2023, by = "iso3") |>
  filter(!is.na(s21), !is.na(s23)) |>
  mutate(
    d1921 = s21 - s19,
    d2123 = s23 - s21,
    d1923 = s23 - s19,
    state = case_when(
      d1921 > 0 & d1923 > 0 & s23 >= s21 ~ "Rose and kept rising",
      d1921 > 0 & d1923 > 0 ~ "Rose, partly reversed, still above 2019",
      d1921 > 0 ~ "Rose, then fell back to or below 2019",
      d1923 > 0 ~ "Did not rise by 2021, above 2019 by 2023",
      .default = "Did not rise, at or below 2019 in 2023"
    )
  )
pandemic_by_group <- pandemic_countries |>
  inner_join(membership, by = "iso3", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  group_by(grouping, key) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    med19 = median(s19),
    med21 = median(s21),
    med23 = median(s23),
    med_d1921 = median(d1921),
    med_d2123 = median(d2123),
    med_d1923 = median(d1923),
    rose = sum(d1921 > 0),
    above19_in23 = sum(d1923 > 0),
    kept = sum(d1921 > 0 & d1923 > 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
pandemic_groups <- groups |>
  select(grouping, key, label) |>
  left_join(pandemic_by_group, by = c("grouping", "key")) |>
  # a group with no country in the panel gets zero counts; its medians stay empty
  mutate(across(
    c(n, rose, above19_in23, kept),
    \(count) coalesce(count, 0L)
  ))

# Pattern counts by income group and by region (latest window), and for income groups by period
pattern_rows <- bind_rows(
  country_windows |>
    filter(has_window) |>
    transmute(period = "W", iso3, pattern, lost_priority),
  select(country_periods, period, iso3, pattern, lost_priority)
)
pattern_by_group <- pattern_rows |>
  inner_join(membership, by = "iso3", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  group_by(period, grouping, key) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    `Economy-led` = sum(pattern == "Economy-led"),
    `Budget-led` = sum(pattern == "Budget-led"),
    `Priority-led` = sum(pattern == "Priority-led"),
    Declining = sum(pattern == "Declining"),
    lost = sum(lost_priority),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
pattern_counts <- groups |>
  select(grouping, key, label) |>
  cross_join(tibble(period = c("W", "P1", "P2", "P3"))) |>
  left_join(pattern_by_group, by = c("period", "grouping", "key")) |>
  mutate(across(
    c(n, `Economy-led`, `Budget-led`, `Priority-led`, Declining, lost),
    \(count) coalesce(count, 0L)
  ))
patterns_income <- pattern_counts |>
  filter(period == "W", grouping %in% c("world", "income")) |>
  select(key, label, n, `Economy-led`, `Budget-led`, `Priority-led`, Declining, lost)
patterns_region <- pattern_counts |>
  filter(period == "W", grouping %in% c("world", "wb_region")) |>
  select(key, label, n, `Economy-led`, `Budget-led`, `Priority-led`, Declining, lost)
patterns_period <- pattern_counts |>
  filter(period != "W", grouping %in% c("world", "income")) |>
  arrange(period) |>
  select(period, key, label, n, `Economy-led`, `Budget-led`, `Priority-led`, Declining, lost)
data.frame(
  `group rows` = nrow(group_summary),
  `largest closure error of a whole` = max(abs(group_summary$agg_closure), na.rm = TRUE),
  `balanced panel` = length(balanced),
  `pandemic panel` = nrow(pandemic_countries),
  check.names = FALSE
)
```

## The prescription for 2027 to 2029

In Section 2, we apply one method to every country with IMF projections. Health's share of government spending, *h*, is held at its value at the end of the country's window (2023 for most countries) through 2026. Government spending in national currency is built from IMF projections: GDP times either the IMF's projected expenditure share (the IMF path) or the 2026 share held flat (the flat path). For each year from 2027 to 2029:

- We define the **ceiling** as all the growth in government spending since 2026, the most the health budget could gain;
- We calculate the **protect amount** as *h* times the ceiling, the increase that keeps health's share where it is and so the least
  to ask for;
- We consider **candidates** that raise *h* by the country's own trend over its window (only if the trend is positive) or by fixed
  steps of +0.25, +0.5 or +0.75 percentage points a year;
- We call a candidate **admissible** if it lies between the protect amount and the ceiling, and set the **upper ask** at the
  largest admissible candidate (the protect amount if none is admissible);
- If government spending does not grow, the method **does not apply**: the question is then the fiscal envelope,
  not health's priority.

We apply the rules in nominal national currency, the unit in which budgets are set. Each amount is also shown in real terms at 2026 prices, using the IMF GDP deflator rebased to 2026, and in US\$ at each year's IMF exchange rate. Cross-country percentages and medians are real: the real increase as a percentage of the 2026 health budget, and the real increase per person in constant 2026 US\$.

```{r engine-prescription}
## Section 2 engine: the ceiling, protect amount, candidates and upper ask for
## every country, path and year 2027-2029.
BASE_YEAR <- 2026
ASK_YEARS <- 2027:2029
CHART_YEARS <- 2024:2029
SHARE_STEPS <- c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75) # steps in health's share, percentage points per year
PATHS <- c(imf = "IMF expenditure path", flat = "Flat spending share")

# the IMF series with one row per country and year and one column per series
weo <- pivot_wider(weo_long, names_from = indicator, values_from = value)

# The base: every country with a window, health's share at the window's end (h), and the share's
# trend over the window in percentage points a year
base <- country_windows |>
  filter(has_window) |>
  transmute(
    iso3, name, income_group, wb_region,
    base_year = y1,
    h = slice1,
    trend = (slice1 - slice0) / (y1 - y0),
    trend_y0 = y0,
    trend_y1 = y1
  )

# Each country from 2024 to 2029 with the IMF series; a year the IMF does not give
# stays empty. We also need the exchange rate (national currency per US$) and the
# price level (2026 = 1) of each year.
imf_years <- base |>
  select(iso3, h) |>
  cross_join(tibble(year = CHART_YEARS)) |>
  left_join(weo, by = c("iso3", "year")) |>
  group_by(iso3) |>
  mutate(
    rate_y = NGDP / NGDPD,
    deflator = NGDP / NGDP_R,
    p = deflator / deflator[year == BASE_YEAR],
    rate26 = rate_y[year == BASE_YEAR],
    share26 = GGX_NGDP[year == BASE_YEAR]
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Government spending on two paths: the IMF's projected expenditure share, or the 2026 share held
# flat from 2027 on; the health budget at the unchanged share follows from either
prescription_lines <- bind_rows(
  mutate(imf_years, variant = "imf", gge_share = GGX_NGDP),
  mutate(imf_years, variant = "flat", gge_share = if_else(year <= BASE_YEAR, GGX_NGDP, share26))
) |>
  mutate(
    gdp = NGDP,
    gge = gdp * gge_share / 100,
    health_protect = gge * h / 100,
    pop = LP
  ) |>
  arrange(iso3, match(variant, names(PATHS)), year) |>
  select(iso3, variant, year, gdp, gge_share, gge, health_protect, h, rate26, rate_y, p, pop)

# Ceiling, protect amount and the four candidates for each country, path and year. A candidate is
# admissible if it lies between the protect amount and the ceiling, and the method applies only
# where government spending grows.
prescription <- prescription_lines |>
  group_by(iso3, variant) |>
  mutate(gge26 = gge[year == BASE_YEAR]) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(year %in% ASK_YEARS) |>
  left_join(select(base, iso3, trend), by = "iso3") |>
  mutate(
    years_ahead = year - BASE_YEAR, # years since 2026
    health26 = gge26 * h / 100, # the 2026 health budget
    d_all = gge - gge26, # ceiling: all new government money to health
    d_protect = h / 100 * d_all, # protect: health's share held
    # the candidates raise health's share each year by the own
    # trend (only if it rose) or a fixed step
    trend_ok = !is.na(trend) & trend > 0,
    c_trend = if_else(trend_ok, gge * (h + trend * years_ahead) / 100 - health26, NA),
    c_025 = gge * (h + SHARE_STEPS[1] * years_ahead) / 100 - health26,
    c_050 = gge * (h + SHARE_STEPS[2] * years_ahead) / 100 - health26,
    c_075 = gge * (h + SHARE_STEPS[3] * years_ahead) / 100 - health26,
    applies = !is.na(d_all) & d_all > 0,
    adm_trend = applies & !is.na(c_trend) & c_trend >= d_protect - 1e-9 & c_trend <= d_all + 1e-9,
    adm_025 = applies & !is.na(c_025) & c_025 >= d_protect - 1e-9 & c_025 <= d_all + 1e-9,
    adm_050 = applies & !is.na(c_050) & c_050 >= d_protect - 1e-9 & c_050 <= d_all + 1e-9,
    adm_075 = applies & !is.na(c_075) & c_075 >= d_protect - 1e-9 & c_075 <= d_all + 1e-9
  )

# The upper ask is the largest admissible candidate (the first one on a tie)
largest_admissible <- prescription |>
  select(iso3, variant, year,
    amount_trend = c_trend, amount_s025 = c_025, amount_s050 = c_050, amount_s075 = c_075,
    adm_trend, adm_s025 = adm_025, adm_s050 = adm_050, adm_s075 = adm_075
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    -c(iso3, variant, year),
    names_to = c(".value", "candidate"), names_sep = "_"
  ) |>
  filter(adm) |>
  group_by(iso3, variant, year) |>
  slice_max(amount, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(iso3, variant, year, best = candidate, best_amount = amount)

# With nothing admissible the ask is the protect amount; where the method does not
# apply there is no ask. We also follow health's share to where the ask takes it,
# and give every amount at 2026 prices.
prescription <- prescription |>
  left_join(largest_admissible, by = c("iso3", "variant", "year")) |>
  mutate(
    setter = case_when(
      !applies ~ "not applicable",
      is.na(best) ~ "none",
      .default = best
    ),
    ask = case_when(
      setter == "none" ~ d_protect,
      setter == "not applicable" ~ NA,
      .default = best_amount
    ),
    h_ask = case_when(
      setter == "trend" ~ h + trend * years_ahead,
      setter == "s025" ~ h + SHARE_STEPS[1] * years_ahead,
      setter == "s050" ~ h + SHARE_STEPS[2] * years_ahead,
      setter == "s075" ~ h + SHARE_STEPS[3] * years_ahead,
      setter == "none" ~ h
    ),
    gge_real = gge / p,
    d_all_real = gge_real - gge26,
    d_protect_real = h / 100 * (gge_real - gge26),
    c_trend_real = if_else(trend_ok, gge_real * (h + trend * years_ahead) / 100 - health26, NA),
    c_025_real = gge_real * (h + SHARE_STEPS[1] * years_ahead) / 100 - health26,
    c_050_real = gge_real * (h + SHARE_STEPS[2] * years_ahead) / 100 - health26,
    c_075_real = gge_real * (h + SHARE_STEPS[3] * years_ahead) / 100 - health26,
    ask_real = gge_real * h_ask / 100 - health26
  ) |>
  left_join(
    select(base, iso3, name, income_group, wb_region, base_year, trend_y0, trend_y1),
    by = "iso3"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    has_data = !is.na(gge26) & !is.na(gge),
    applies = if_else(has_data, applies, NA),
    setter = if_else(has_data, setter, "no IMF projection")
  )

# Units: nominal US$ at each year's rate, the real rise in % of the 2026 health budget (and the
# nominal one), and real US$ per person in constant 2026 US$
for (amount in c("d_all", "d_protect", "ask", "c_trend", "c_025", "c_050", "c_075")) {
  nominal <- prescription[[amount]]
  real <- prescription[[paste0(amount, "_real")]]
  prescription[[paste0(amount, "_usd")]] <- nominal / prescription$rate_y
  prescription[[paste0(amount, "_pct_nominal")]] <- 100 * nominal / prescription$health26
  prescription[[paste0(amount, "_pct")]] <- 100 * real / prescription$health26
  prescription[[paste0(amount, "_usd_pp")]] <- real / prescription$rate26 / prescription$pop
}

setter_lab <- c(
  trend = "Own trend", s025 = "+0.25 a year", s050 = "+0.5 a year", s075 = "+0.75 a year",
  none = "No admissible increase", "not applicable" = "Does not apply",
  "no IMF projection" = "No IMF projection"
)
prescription <- prescription |>
  mutate(
    real_ceiling_pos = d_all_real > 0,
    ask_share_of_ceiling = if_else(real_ceiling_pos, 100 * ask_real / d_all_real, NA),
    ask_share_of_ceiling_nominal = 100 * ask / d_all,
    ask_above_real_ceiling = applies & real_ceiling_pos & ask_real > d_all_real,
    closure_low = ask - d_protect, # check: zero or more where the method applies
    closure_high = d_all - ask, # check: zero or more where the method applies
    setter_label = unname(setter_lab[setter])
  ) |>
  arrange(iso3, variant, year)

# Group medians for both paths and every year; the upper ask counts only where the method applies
prescription_by_group <- prescription |>
  filter(has_data) |>
  inner_join(membership, by = "iso3", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  group_by(grouping, key, variant, year) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_applies = sum(applies),
    n_not_applies = sum(!applies),
    med_d_all_pct = median(d_all_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    med_d_protect_pct = median(d_protect_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    med_ask_pct = median(ask_pct[applies], na.rm = TRUE),
    med_d_all_usd_pp = median(d_all_usd_pp, na.rm = TRUE),
    med_d_protect_usd_pp = median(d_protect_usd_pp, na.rm = TRUE),
    med_ask_usd_pp = median(ask_usd_pp[applies], na.rm = TRUE),
    med_ask_share_of_ceiling = median(ask_share_of_ceiling[applies], na.rm = TRUE),
    n_real = sum(!is.na(d_all_pct)),
    n_real_ceiling_not_pos = sum(!real_ceiling_pos, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_real_fall_only = sum(applies & !real_ceiling_pos, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_ask_above_real_ceiling = sum(ask_above_real_ceiling[applies], na.rm = TRUE),
    set_trend = sum(applies & setter == "trend"),
    set_025 = sum(applies & setter == "s025"),
    set_050 = sum(applies & setter == "s050"),
    set_075 = sum(applies & setter == "s075"),
    set_none = sum(applies & setter == "none"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
prescription_groups <- groups |>
  select(grouping, key, label) |>
  cross_join(tibble(variant = names(PATHS))) |>
  cross_join(tibble(year = ASK_YEARS)) |>
  left_join(prescription_by_group, by = c("grouping", "key", "variant", "year")) |>
  # a group with no country in a year gets zero counts; its medians stay empty
  mutate(across(
    c(n, starts_with("n_"), starts_with("set_")),
    \(count) coalesce(count, 0L)
  ))

applying <- filter(prescription, has_data, applies %in% TRUE)
data.frame(
  countries = length(unique(prescription$iso3)),
  `with IMF projections` = length(unique(prescription$iso3[prescription$has_data])),
  `ask below protect (should be 0)` = sum(applying$closure_low < -1e-6),
  `ask above ceiling (should be 0)` = sum(applying$closure_high < -1e-6),
  check.names = FALSE
)
```

## From the engine to the slides

Each slide chunk below reads one list of tables, `mine`, which we build here from the engine's objects. The same slide
chunks are run in the final chunk on the report's own output tables, which carry the same columns, so the check
compares like with like. The labels in this chunk only name groups and periods; none of them computes anything new.

```{r slide-helpers}
## The bundle of tables every slide reads, the names of the matching report outputs, the labels the
## slides print and the country names they use.
mine <- list(
  win = country_windows,
  per = country_periods,
  grp = group_summary,
  nf_med = medians_without_flagged,
  nf_agg = wholes_without_flagged,
  trend = trends,
  pand = pandemic_countries,
  pand_grp = pandemic_groups,
  pat_inc = patterns_income,
  pat_reg = patterns_region,
  pat_per = patterns_period,
  contrib = contributions,
  rx = prescription,
  rx_lines = prescription_lines,
  rx_grp = prescription_groups
)
# the report's tables are plain data frames, so we hand the slides plain data frames too
mine <- lapply(mine, as.data.frame)
REF_NAMES <- c(
  win = "country_window_decomposition",
  per = "country_period_decomposition",
  grp = "group_decomposition",
  nf_med = "group_window_medians_without_flagged",
  nf_agg = "group_aggregates_2013_2023_without_flagged",
  trend = "trends_2000_2023",
  pand = "health_priority_pandemic_countries",
  pand_grp = "health_priority_pandemic_groups",
  pat_inc = "patterns_by_income",
  pat_reg = "patterns_by_region",
  pat_per = "patterns_by_period_income",
  contrib = "income_group_contributions_2013_2023",
  rx = "prescription_country_year",
  rx_lines = "prescription_lines_2024_2029",
  rx_grp = "prescription_groups"
)

INC <- inc_levels
INC_LABEL <- c(
  low = "Low income", lower_middle = "Lower middle income", upper_middle = "Upper middle income",
  high = "High income"
)
INC_CODE <- c(low = "Low", lower_middle = "LM", upper_middle = "UM", high = "High")
REG <- reg_levels[reg_levels != "not_classified"]
REG_LABEL <- c(
  "East Asia & Pacific" = "East Asia and Pacific",
  "Europe & Central Asia" = "Europe and Central Asia",
  "Latin America & Caribbean" = "Latin America and the Caribbean",
  "Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan" =
    "Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan",
  "North America" = "North America",
  "South Asia" = "South Asia",
  "Sub-Saharan Africa" = "Sub-Saharan Africa",
  "Not classified" = "No World Bank region"
)
PERIOD_LABEL <- c(P1 = "2000-2010", P2 = "2010-2019", P3 = "2019-2023")

# The country names the slides print: a shorter form for fourteen countries, otherwise the GHED name
# without its bracket. We sort names without their accents, as the deck does, so Türkiye sits among
# the T's whatever the computer's locale.
SHORT_NAME <- c(
  PSE = "occupied Palestinian territory", VCT = "St. Vincent and the Grenadines",
  NLD = "Netherlands", FSM = "Micronesia", LAO = "Lao PDR", GBR = "United Kingdom",
  USA = "United States", COD = "DR Congo", TZA = "Tanzania", SYR = "Syria", KOR = "Korea, Rep.",
  PRK = "Korea, DPR", MDA = "Moldova", ARE = "United Arab Emirates"
)
short_names <- countries |>
  mutate(
    name_without_bracket = trimws(sub("\\s*\\(.*\\)\\s*$", "", name)),
    short = coalesce(unname(SHORT_NAME[iso3]), name_without_bracket),
    sort_name = tolower(chartr("ôüéçãíáóÔÜÉ", "ouecaiaooue", short))
  ) |>
  select(iso3, short, sort_name)
```

# The deck

## Cover. What accounted for the change in government health spending, 2000 to 2023

*Kicker on the slide: Global decomposition.*

On the cover, we show the title, a subtitle naming the three parts, and the questions the deck answers: how much of the
change in government health spending per person came from the economy, from a larger government budget and from a
larger share of the budget for health; where health lost ground; and how much the health budget could ask for in 2027
to 2029. The cover's count of countries with a window and its data sources come from the chunks that follow, so no
computation sits here.

# Section 1. The decomposition, 2000-2023

## Slide 1. Three parts of government health spending per person

*Question on the slide: Where can more public money for health come from?*

On the first slide, we set out the identity and fill in the three parts with world levels. The countries with all three parts in
every year from 2000 to 2023 are taken as one block: summed real GDP over summed population gives GDP per person, summed
government spending over summed GDP gives the size of government, and summed government health spending over summed
government spending gives health's share. The product of the three equals government health spending per person, in
2000 and in 2023.

We use the chart to show the change from 2013 to 2023 for every country with all parts and population in both years, again as one
block, and split the change into the three parts. The bars are stacked as a waterfall: each part starts where the previous one
ends, and the last bar is the total. The shares under the chart divide the economy part and the health priority part by
the total.

We show two sets of countries on the slide. The levels need every year from 2000 to 2023 and the change needs only 2013 and
2023, so the change covers more countries than the levels.

```{r slide-01-identity, results = "asis", fig.height = 4.6}
## Slide 1: the identity in levels for the balanced panel as a whole (2000, 2023), and the world's
## 2013-2023 change split into the three parts.
# the balanced panel as a whole in 2000 and 2023
world_trend <- filter(mine$trend, key == "world")
levels_2000 <- filter(world_trend, year == 2000)
levels_2023 <- filter(world_trend, year == 2023)

# the world as a whole from 2013 to 2023: the three parts and the total, in that order
world <- filter(mine$grp, key == "world", period == "W")
parts <- c(world$agg_econ, world$agg_budget, world$agg_priority, world$agg_total)

identity_levels <- tibble(
  Part = c(
    "GDP per person", "Government spending, % of GDP", "Health, % of government spending",
    "Government health spending per person"
  ),
  `2000` = c(
    dollars(levels_2000$agg_gdp), share_pct(levels_2000$agg_pie),
    share_pct(levels_2000$agg_slice), dollars(levels_2000$agg_ghe)
  ),
  `2023` = c(
    dollars(levels_2023$agg_gdp), share_pct(levels_2023$agg_pie),
    share_pct(levels_2023$agg_slice), dollars(levels_2023$agg_ghe)
  )
)
world_change <- tibble(
  Part = unname(PART_LABEL),
  `Log points a year` = signed(parts)
)
slide_counts <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Countries with all parts in every year, 2000-2023",
    "Countries with all parts in 2013 and 2023",
    "Share of the change from the economy",
    "Share of the change from health priority"
  ),
  Value = c(
    levels_2000$n_bal,
    world$n_agg,
    whole_pct(100 * world$agg_econ / world$agg_total),
    whole_pct(100 * world$agg_priority / world$agg_total)
  )
)
tables <- list(
  "The identity in levels, countries with all parts in every year, as a whole (constant 2023 US$)" =
    identity_levels,
  "The world's change, 2013-2023, as a whole (log points a year)" = world_change,
  "Counts and shares printed on the slide" = slide_counts
)
show_tables(tables)

# The waterfall: each part starts where the previous one ends, and the last bar is the total
steps <- tibble(
  x = 1:4,
  part = factor(unname(PART_LABEL), levels = unname(PART_LABEL)),
  from = c(0, parts[1], parts[1] + parts[2], 0),
  to = c(parts[1], parts[1] + parts[2], parts[1] + parts[2] + parts[3], parts[4]),
  bottom = pmin(from, to),
  top = pmax(from, to),
  label = signed(parts)
)
ggplot(steps) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = x - 0.35, xmax = x + 0.35, ymin = bottom, ymax = top, fill = part)) +
  geom_text(aes(x = x, y = top + 0.08, label = label),
    vjust = 0, size = 3.6, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:4, labels = levels(steps$part)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PART_FILL, guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 3)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Log points a year", title = "The world's change, 2013-2023, as a whole",
    subtitle = paste(
      world$n_agg, "countries with all parts in 2013 and 2023; the three parts add up to the total"
    )
  )
```

## Slide 2. Real government health spending per person, 2000 to 2023

*Question on the slide: How much did government health spending per person grow?*

We follow real government health spending per person from 2000 to 2023 in two ways. The solid line is the
median of the balanced panel, the countries with all three parts in every year, with the middle half of those countries
shaded. The dashed line takes the same countries as one block: their summed spending over their summed population.
Keeping one fixed set of countries means the lines move only because spending moved, not because countries entered or
left the data. The note under the chart gives the median of all countries with data in a given year for comparison.

We use a different statistic for the "median country grew ... log points a year" in the lead. Each country's 23-year rate is the
year-weighted average of its three period rates (10, 9 and 4 years), which is exact for log points, and the median is
taken across those countries. The panel on the right of the slide, repeated in the second table, gives the median by
income group; the high-to-low ratio divides the high-income group's spending per person by the low-income group's, both
as wholes.

We use the median and the whole to answer different questions. The whole follows the large high-income spenders, while the
median follows a typical country, so the gap between the two lines is itself part of the finding.

```{r slide-02-trend, results = "asis"}
## Slide 2: the trend 2000-2023 (median, middle half, as a whole), the median country's 23-year
## rate, income-group medians and the high-to-low ratio.
world_trend <- mine$trend |>
  filter(key == "world") |>
  arrange(year)
world_2000 <- filter(world_trend, year == 2000)
world_2019 <- filter(world_trend, year == 2019)
world_2020 <- filter(world_trend, year == 2020)
world_2022 <- filter(world_trend, year == 2022)
world_2023 <- filter(world_trend, year == 2023)

# Each country's 23-year rate is the year-weighted average of its three period rates (10, 9 and 4
# years), which is exact for log points; we take the countries with all three periods
country_rates <- mine$per |>
  select(iso3, period, total) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = period, values_from = total) |>
  filter(!is.na(P1), !is.na(P2), !is.na(P3)) |>
  mutate(rate_23 = (10 * P1 + 9 * P2 + 4 * P3) / 23) |>
  left_join(select(mine$win, iso3, income_group), by = "iso3")
low_rates <- filter(country_rates, income_group == "low")
median_rate <- median(country_rates$rate_23)

# the income groups in 2000 and 2023: the median country, and the high-to-low ratio of the wholes
income_trend <- mine$trend |>
  filter(grouping == "income") |>
  arrange(match(key, INC))
income_2000 <- filter(income_trend, year == 2000)
income_2023 <- filter(income_trend, year == 2023)
ratio_2000 <- income_2000$agg_ghe[income_2000$key == "high"] /
  income_2000$agg_ghe[income_2000$key == "low"]
ratio_2023 <- income_2023$agg_ghe[income_2023$key == "high"] /
  income_2023$agg_ghe[income_2023$key == "low"]

world_table <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Countries with data in every year (balanced panel)", "Median, 2000", "Median, 2023",
    "Median country's change, 2000-2023, log points a year", "As a whole, 2000", "As a whole, 2023",
    "Countries spending less per person in 2023 than in 2000", "As a whole, 2019",
    "As a whole, 2020", "Median, 2022", "All countries with data: median, 2000",
    "All countries with data: countries, 2000", "All countries with data: median, 2023",
    "All countries with data: countries, 2023"
  ),
  Value = c(
    world_2000$n_bal,
    dollars(world_2000$med_ghe_bal),
    dollars(world_2023$med_ghe_bal),
    one_decimal(abs(median_rate)),
    dollars(world_2000$agg_ghe),
    dollars(world_2023$agg_ghe),
    sum(country_rates$rate_23 < 0),
    dollars(world_2019$agg_ghe),
    dollars(world_2020$agg_ghe),
    dollars(world_2022$med_ghe_bal),
    dollars(world_2000$med_ghe),
    world_2000$n,
    dollars(world_2023$med_ghe),
    world_2023$n
  )
)
income_table <- tibble(
  `Income group` = c(
    unname(INC_LABEL),
    "High to low, groups as a whole",
    "Low income: spent less in 2023 than in 2000"
  ),
  `2000` = c(dollars(income_2000$med_ghe), paste(round(ratio_2000), "to one"), ""),
  `2023` = c(
    dollars(income_2023$med_ghe),
    paste(round(ratio_2023), "to one"),
    paste(sum(low_rates$rate_23 < 0), "of", nrow(low_rates))
  )
)
tables <- list(
  "World, constant 2023 US$ per person" = world_table,
  "Income groups" = income_table
)
show_tables(tables)

# the two lines end with their 2023 value
line_ends <- tibble(
  year = 2023,
  y = c(world_2023$agg_ghe, world_2023$med_ghe_bal),
  label = c(
    paste("As a whole", dollars(world_2023$agg_ghe)),
    paste("Median", dollars(world_2023$med_ghe_bal))
  )
)
ggplot(world_trend, aes(year)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p25_ghe_bal, ymax = p75_ghe_bal), fill = WB[["tint"]]) +
  geom_line(aes(y = agg_ghe), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = med_ghe_bal), colour = WB[["navy"]], linewidth = 1.3) +
  geom_text(
    data = line_ends, aes(x = year + 0.4, y = y, label = label),
    hjust = 0, size = 3.4, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  annotate("text",
    x = 2000.5, y = 16, label = "Shaded: middle half of countries (25th to 75th percentile)",
    hjust = 0, size = 3.2, colour = WB[["slate"]]
  ) +
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = c(10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000), limits = c(10, 2000),
    labels = scales::label_comma(prefix = "US$")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2023), expand = expansion(add = c(0.3, 7))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Constant 2023 US$ per person, log scale",
    title = paste0("World, ", world_2000$n_bal, " countries with data in every year")
  )
```

## Slide 3. Growth and its three parts by period, world

*Question on the slide: Is the economy still carrying the growth?*

We compare three fixed periods, 2000-2010, 2010-2019 and 2019-2023. The chart takes the world as one block in
each period (every country with all parts and population at both ends of the period), so its three parts add up to the
total. The table gives the median country, where each part's median is taken across countries on its own, so the part
medians need not add up to the median total. The count of economy-led countries in each period follows the pattern rule
explained under slide 7.

We calculate each period rate as an average over the years in the period. The last period is only four years long and includes the
pandemic jump and its partial reversal, so one unusual year weighs more in its rates than in the two longer periods. A falling economy part in the
median country is the main reading of the slide; whether the budget parts can keep growth going without the economy is
the question the rest of Section 1 takes up.

```{r slide-03-periods, results = "asis", fig.height = 4.4}
## Slide 3: the world by fixed period, as a whole (chart) and as the median country (table), and the
## count of economy-led countries per period.
world_periods <- mine$grp |>
  filter(key == "world", period %in% c("P1", "P2", "P3")) |>
  arrange(period)
world_patterns <- mine$pat_per |>
  filter(key == "world") |>
  arrange(period)

median_country <- tibble(
  Period = unname(PERIOD_LABEL),
  Economy = signed(world_periods$med_econ),
  `Size of government` = signed(world_periods$med_budget),
  `Health priority` = signed(world_periods$med_priority),
  Total = signed(world_periods$med_total),
  n = world_periods$n_med
)
world_whole <- tibble(
  Period = unname(PERIOD_LABEL),
  Economy = signed(world_periods$agg_econ),
  `Size of government` = signed(world_periods$agg_budget),
  `Health priority` = signed(world_periods$agg_priority),
  Total = signed(world_periods$agg_total),
  Countries = world_periods$n_agg
)
economy_led <- tibble(
  Period = unname(PERIOD_LABEL),
  `Economy-led` = world_patterns$`Economy-led`,
  Countries = world_patterns$n
)
tables <- list(
  "Median country, log points a year (each part's median taken separately)" = median_country,
  "World as a whole, log points a year (the parts add up)" = world_whole,
  "Economy-led countries by period" = economy_led
)
show_tables(tables)

whole <- tibble(
  label = paste0(PERIOD_LABEL, "\n", world_periods$n_agg, " countries"),
  econ = world_periods$agg_econ,
  budget = world_periods$agg_budget,
  priority = world_periods$agg_priority,
  total = world_periods$agg_total
)
plot_parts(whole, "label") +
  labs(title = "World as a whole: the three parts add up to the total")
```

## Slide 4. Growth and its three parts by income group, latest ten-year window

*Question on the slide: Which income groups grew, and from which part?*

We repeat the split for the four income groups over the latest window. The table reports the median country, using each country's own window (2013-2023 for most). The chart reports each group as a whole for the fixed years 2013 and 2023, because an aggregate needs the same years for every member. The third table shows the largest member's share of group government health spending in 2023, calculated as spending per person times population.

Large members shape a group taken as a whole: India in lower middle income, China in upper middle income and the United
States in high income. A whole that grows fast can therefore mostly reflect one country, and a whole that falls can hide
a typical country that grew, which is what slide 6 shows for low income.

```{r slide-04-income, results = "asis", fig.height = 4.8}
## Slide 4: income groups over the latest window, the median country (table) and each group as a
## whole 2013-2023 (chart), and the largest member's share of each group's spending.
income_rows <- mine$grp |>
  filter(period == "W", key %in% c("world", INC)) |>
  arrange(match(key, c("world", INC)))
group_names <- c("World", unname(INC_LABEL))

# the largest member of each income group and its share of the group's spending in 2023
largest <- mine$contrib |>
  filter(income_group %in% INC) |>
  group_by(income_group) |>
  mutate(share = 100 * ghe1_musd / sum(ghe1_musd)) |>
  slice_max(ghe1_musd, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(match(income_group, INC)) |>
  left_join(short_names, by = "iso3") |>
  transmute(
    `Income group` = unname(INC_LABEL[income_group]),
    `Largest member` = short,
    `Share of the group's spending, 2023` = whole_pct(share)
  )

median_country <- tibble(
  `Income group` = group_names,
  Economy = signed(income_rows$med_econ),
  `Size of government` = signed(income_rows$med_budget),
  `Health priority` = signed(income_rows$med_priority),
  Total = signed(income_rows$med_total),
  n = income_rows$n_med
)
group_whole <- tibble(
  `Income group` = group_names,
  Economy = signed(income_rows$agg_econ),
  `Size of government` = signed(income_rows$agg_budget),
  `Health priority` = signed(income_rows$agg_priority),
  Total = signed(income_rows$agg_total),
  Countries = income_rows$n_agg
)
tables <- list(
  "Median country, own latest window, log points a year (parts taken separately)" = median_country,
  "Group as a whole, 2013-2023, log points a year (the parts add up)" = group_whole,
  "Largest member of each income group" = largest
)
show_tables(tables)

whole <- tibble(
  label = paste0(group_names, "\n", income_rows$n_agg, " countries"),
  econ = income_rows$agg_econ,
  budget = income_rows$agg_budget,
  priority = income_rows$agg_priority,
  total = income_rows$agg_total
)
plot_parts(whole, "label", xlab = "Average annual change, log points, 2013-2023") +
  labs(title = "Each income group as a whole, 2013-2023: the three parts add up")
```

## Slide 5. Growth and its three parts by World Bank region, latest ten-year window

*Question on the slide: Where did growth come from, region by region?*

We put the seven World Bank regions in one heat table: the median country on the left (own window) and the
region as a whole on the right (2013-2023), each with the three parts and the total. Blue cells added to spending per
person and rust cells subtracted, darker for larger values. North America (two countries) and South Asia (six) have
fewer than eight countries, so the two regions are shown but not compared, in paler rows. The bar chart on the right of
the slide, given here as the second table, counts the countries in each region whose spending per person fell over
their window.

A region's median and its whole can point in different directions, most clearly in East Asia and Pacific, where the
economy accounts for most of the whole's growth while health priority adds more in the median country.

```{r slide-05-regions, results = "asis", fig.height = 5}
## Slide 5: World Bank regions over the latest window, median country and region as a whole, and the
## share of countries whose spending per person fell.
region_rows <- mine$grp |>
  filter(period == "W", key %in% c("world", REG)) |>
  arrange(match(key, c("world", REG)))
region_names <- c("World", unname(REG_LABEL[REG]))
# regions with fewer than eight countries are described, not compared
compared <- grepl("^Carries", region_rows$status)

heat <- tibble(
  Region = region_names,
  Countries = region_rows$n_med,
  Compared = if_else(compared, "yes", "described only"),
  `Median: Economy` = signed(region_rows$med_econ),
  `Median: Size of government` = signed(region_rows$med_budget),
  `Median: Health priority` = signed(region_rows$med_priority),
  `Median: Total` = signed(region_rows$med_total),
  `Whole: Economy` = signed(region_rows$agg_econ),
  `Whole: Size of government` = signed(region_rows$agg_budget),
  `Whole: Health priority` = signed(region_rows$agg_priority),
  `Whole: Total` = signed(region_rows$agg_total)
)

# countries whose spending per person fell over their window, the highest share first
fell <- mine$pat_reg |>
  filter(key %in% REG) |>
  arrange(match(key, REG)) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * Declining / n)) |>
  arrange(desc(pct), desc(n))
fell_table <- tibble(
  Region = unname(REG_LABEL[fell$key]),
  Declining = paste(fell$Declining, "of", fell$n),
  Share = paste0(fell$pct, "%")
)

tables <- list(
  "Log points a year: median country (own window) and region as a whole (2013-2023)" = heat,
  "Countries whose spending per person fell over their window" = fell_table
)
show_tables(tables)

# The heat table as a chart: one tile per region, block and part. The colour
# scale stops at 4 log points either way.
heat_long <- region_rows |>
  mutate(
    region = factor(region_names, levels = rev(region_names)),
    compared = compared
  ) |>
  select(
    region, compared, med_econ, med_budget, med_priority, med_total,
    agg_econ, agg_budget, agg_priority, agg_total
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    -c(region, compared),
    names_to = c("block", "part"), names_sep = "_", values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    block = if_else(block == "med", "Median country", "Region as a whole, 2013-2023"),
    part = factor(unname(PART_LABEL[part]), levels = unname(PART_LABEL)),
    fill = pmin(pmax(value, -4), 4),
    label = signed(value)
  )
ggplot(heat_long, aes(x = part, y = region)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = fill, alpha = compared), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 3.2) +
  facet_wrap(~block) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = WB[["rust"]], mid = "white", high = WB[["blue"]], midpoint = 0, guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1, `FALSE` = 0.4), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Economy", "Govt size", "Priority", "Total")) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Log points a year, by World Bank region",
    caption = paste(
      "Blue added to spending per person, rust subtracted.",
      "Paler rows: fewer than 8 countries, shown, not compared.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

## Slide 6. Low-income countries: change in spending, 2013 to 2023

*Question on the slide: Why do the typical low-income country and the group as a whole disagree?*

We find that the low-income median country grew, while the group as a whole fell. Each bar shows one country's change in annual government health spending from 2013 to 2023, in US\$ million at 2023 prices (spending per person times population, for countries with all parts and population in both years). Rust marks countries whose series carries a data flag. Group spending grew more slowly than population, so spending per person for the group as a whole fell; three flagged countries (Syria, Sudan and Yemen) account for most of the loss.

We use the statistics table to show both summaries with and without the flagged countries. Both statements on the slide are
true at once: the typical low-income government raised spending per person, while the group's combined spending per
person fell. A few large losses in money terms can outweigh many small gains.

```{r slide-06-low-income, results = "asis", fig.height = 6.4}
## Slide 6: each low-income country's change in annual spending 2013-2023 (US$
## million, 2023 prices), the group's spending and population, and the median and
## whole with and without flagged countries.
low_income <- filter(mine$contrib, income_group == "low")
spend_2013 <- sum(low_income$ghe0_musd)
spend_2023 <- sum(low_income$ghe1_musd)
pop_2013 <- sum(low_income$pop0_m)
pop_2023 <- sum(low_income$pop1_m)

# each country's change, smallest first, printed whole with its sign
low <- low_income |>
  left_join(short_names, by = "iso3") |>
  mutate(
    change = ghe1_musd - ghe0_musd,
    rounded_change = round(change),
    change_label = scales::comma(change, accuracy = 1, style_positive = "plus")
  ) |>
  arrange(change)
gains <- low |>
  filter(rounded_change > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(rounded_change))
# Syria, Sudan and Yemen: their spending in 2013 and 2023, and what the three lost together
three <- low |>
  filter(iso3 %in% c("SYR", "SDN", "YEM")) |>
  mutate(
    printed_2013 = scales::comma(ghe0_musd, accuracy = 1),
    printed_2023 = scales::comma(ghe1_musd, accuracy = 1),
    range = paste(printed_2013, "to", printed_2023)
  )
lost_by_three <- -sum(three$change)

# countries whose window carries a data flag
flagged <- mine$win |>
  filter(!is.na(total), !is.na(flag), nzchar(flag)) |>
  pull(iso3)

# the median country and the group as a whole, with and without the flagged countries
low_all <- filter(mine$grp, key == "low", period == "W")
low_median_no_flag <- filter(mine$nf_med, key == "low")
low_whole_no_flag <- filter(mine$nf_agg, key == "low")

group_table <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Countries", "Spending, US$ million, 2013", "Spending, US$ million, 2023", "Change in spending",
    "Population, million, 2013", "Population, million, 2023", "Change in population",
    "Spending lost by Syria, Sudan and Yemen, US$ million", "Syria, US$ million, 2013 and 2023",
    "Sudan, US$ million, 2013 and 2023", "Yemen, US$ million, 2013 and 2023", "Largest gains"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(low),
    scales::comma(spend_2013, accuracy = 1),
    scales::comma(spend_2023, accuracy = 1),
    paste0("+", round(100 * (spend_2023 / spend_2013 - 1)), "%"),
    scales::comma(pop_2013, accuracy = 1),
    scales::comma(pop_2023, accuracy = 1),
    paste0("+", round(100 * (pop_2023 / pop_2013 - 1)), "%"),
    scales::comma(lost_by_three, accuracy = 1),
    three$range[three$iso3 == "SYR"],
    three$range[three$iso3 == "SDN"],
    three$range[three$iso3 == "YEM"],
    knitr::combine_words(gains$short[1:4], oxford_comma = FALSE)
  )
)
two_statistics <- tibble(
  Statistic = c(
    "Median country", "Group as a whole", "Median, without flagged countries",
    "As a whole, without flagged countries"
  ),
  Countries = c(low_all$n_med, low_all$n_agg, low_median_no_flag$n_med, low_whole_no_flag$n_agg),
  `Log points a year` = signed(c(
    low_all$med_total, low_all$agg_total, low_median_no_flag$med_total, low_whole_no_flag$agg_total
  ))
)
by_country <- tibble(
  Country = low$short,
  Change = low$change_label,
  Flag = if_else(low$iso3 %in% flagged, "flagged", "")
)
tables <- list(
  "The low-income group, 2013 and 2023" = group_table,
  "Two statistics, with and without flagged countries (low income, latest window)" = two_statistics,
  "Change in annual spending by country, US$ million at 2023 prices" = by_country
)
show_tables(tables)

low_chart <- low |>
  mutate(
    country = factor(short, levels = rev(short)),
    flag_status = if_else(iso3 %in% flagged, "Series carries a data flag", "No data flag"),
    label_hjust = if_else(change < 0, 1.1, -0.1)
  )
ggplot(low_chart, aes(x = change, y = country, fill = flag_status)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = change_label, hjust = label_hjust), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("No data flag" = WB[["blue"]], "Series carries a data flag" = WB[["rust"]])
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
```
