    limits = c(-650, 450), breaks = seq(-600, 400, 200),
    labels = scales::label_number(style_positive = "plus")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Change in annual spending, US$ million at 2023 prices", y = NULL,
    title = paste(
      "The", nrow(low), "low-income countries with all parts and population in 2013 and 2023"
    )
  )
```

## Slide 7. Four patterns of change, latest ten-year window and three periods

*Question on the slide: Did countries grow through the economy or through the budget?*

We assign each country one of four pattern names. A country is declining if spending per person fell over the window;
otherwise the pattern is named after the largest of the three parts: economy-led, budget-led (size of government) or
priority-led (health's share). The names describe the arithmetic, not a cause. The first table counts the patterns over
the latest window by income group, the second does the same for the world in each fixed period, and the third follows
countries from 2010-2019 into 2019-2023.

We find that countries change pattern often between periods, so a pattern says more about a decade than about a country's lasting
character. Budget-led and priority-led countries together outnumber the economy-led ones over the latest window.

```{r slide-07-patterns, results = "asis", fig.height = 4.6}
## Slide 7: pattern counts by income group (latest window) and by period (world), and how often a
## country's pattern changed between 2010-2019 and 2019-2023.
PATTERNS <- c("Economy-led", "Budget-led", "Priority-led", "Declining")
by_income <- mine$pat_inc |>
  filter(key %in% c("world", INC)) |>
  arrange(match(key, c("world", INC)))
world_by_period <- mine$pat_per |>
  filter(key == "world") |>
  arrange(period)
# the three periods, then the latest window
by_period <- bind_rows(world_by_period, by_income[1, ]) |>
  select(n, all_of(PATTERNS))

# countries with a 2010-2019 and a 2019-2023 decomposition, and
# the pattern of each in the two periods
patterns_2010s <- mine$per |>
  filter(period == "P2") |>
  select(iso3, pattern_2010s = pattern)
patterns_pandemic <- mine$per |>
  filter(period == "P3") |>
  select(iso3, pattern_pandemic = pattern)
moved <- inner_join(patterns_2010s, patterns_pandemic, by = "iso3")
europe <- filter(mine$pat_reg, key == "Europe & Central Asia")
africa <- filter(mine$pat_reg, key == "Sub-Saharan Africa")
world <- by_income[1, ]

income_table <- tibble(
  Group = c("World", unname(INC_LABEL)),
  n = by_income$n,
  `Economy-led` = by_income$`Economy-led`,
  `Budget-led` = by_income$`Budget-led`,
  `Priority-led` = by_income$`Priority-led`,
  Declining = by_income$Declining,
  `Share declining` = c("", whole_pct(100 * by_income$Declining[-1] / by_income$n[-1]))
)
period_table <- tibble(
  Group = c(unname(PERIOD_LABEL), "Latest window"),
  n = by_period$n,
  `Economy-led` = by_period$`Economy-led`,
  `Budget-led` = by_period$`Budget-led`,
  `Priority-led` = by_period$`Priority-led`,
  Declining = by_period$Declining
)
movement_table <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Countries with both 2010-2019 and 2019-2023", "Changed pattern", "Economy-led in 2010-2019",
    "Still economy-led in 2019-2023", "Budget-led or priority-led, latest window",
    "Economy-led, latest window", "Europe and Central Asia: economy-led",
    "Sub-Saharan Africa: declining"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(moved),
    sum(moved$pattern_2010s != moved$pattern_pandemic),
    sum(moved$pattern_2010s == "Economy-led"),
    sum(moved$pattern_2010s == "Economy-led" & moved$pattern_pandemic == "Economy-led"),
    world$`Budget-led` + world$`Priority-led`,
    world$`Economy-led`,
    paste(europe$`Economy-led`, "of", europe$n),
    paste(africa$Declining, "of", africa$n)
  )
)
tables <- list(
  "Patterns by income group, latest window (countries)" = income_table,
  "Patterns by period, world (countries)" = period_table,
  "Movement between periods and other counts on the slide" = movement_table
)
show_tables(tables)

# one bar per group, split into the four patterns as shares of the group's countries
group_order <- c("World", unname(INC_LABEL), unname(PERIOD_LABEL), "Latest window")
shares <- bind_rows(
  mutate(
    by_income,
    panel = "By income group, latest window",
    group = c("World", unname(INC_LABEL))
  ),
  mutate(
    by_period,
    panel = "World, by period",
    group = c(unname(PERIOD_LABEL), "Latest window")
  )
) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(PATTERNS), names_to = "pattern", values_to = "count") |>
  mutate(
    pattern = factor(pattern, levels = rev(PATTERNS)),
    group = factor(group, levels = rev(group_order)),
    # we write the count on segments of four countries or more, in black on the light blue
    label = if_else(count >= 4, as.character(count), ""),
    label_colour = if_else(pattern == "Budget-led", "black", "white")
  )
ggplot(shares, aes(x = 100 * count / n, y = group, fill = pattern)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label, colour = label_colour, group = pattern),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 3
  ) +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Economy-led" = "#8f99a3", "Budget-led" = "#7fc4ea", "Priority-led" = "#0071bc",
      Declining = "#b5452c"
    ),
    breaks = PATTERNS
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100), labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Share of countries (labels: countries)", y = NULL, title = "Four patterns of change")
```

## Slide 8. Economy part against health priority part, by country

*Question on the slide: Where did health lose budget share while the economy grew?*

We plot each country as a point over its latest window: the economy part on the horizontal axis and the health priority part on
the vertical axis, both in log points a year. The lower right quarter, shaded, holds the countries where health's share
of government spending fell while real GDP per person grew; those countries are drawn in rust and named by income group
in the second table. The four counts in the corners come from the signs alone, so a country on an axis line is counted
on the side the rule puts it.

Our chart shows the range containing most countries, while the corner counts include countries outside that range. A falling health share in a growing economy does not always mean spending fell. In many countries with a falling share, the economy part exceeded the loss of priority, so spending per person still rose. The slide therefore treats the share and the total as separate measures.

```{r slide-08-quadrants, results = "asis", fig.height = 5.6}
## Slide 8: the economy part against the health priority part for every country with a window, the
## four sign quadrants, and the countries where health lost priority while the economy grew.
win <- mine$win |>
  filter(!is.na(total)) |>
  left_join(short_names, by = "iso3")
econ <- win$econ
prio <- win$priority
total <- win$total
lost <- win$lost_priority %in% TRUE

# the countries where health lost priority while the economy grew, by income group, alphabetical
lost_count <- c()
lost_names <- c()
for (group in INC) {
  in_group <- win |>
    filter(lost_priority %in% TRUE, income_group == group) |>
    arrange(sort_name)
  lost_count[group] <- nrow(in_group)
  lost_names[group] <- knitr::combine_words(in_group$short, oxford_comma = FALSE)
}

counts <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Countries with a window", "Economy up, health share up or flat",
    "Economy up, health share down (health lost priority)",
    "Economy flat or down, health share up or flat", "Both down",
    "Lost priority and still spent more per person", "Lost priority and spent less per person",
    "Health share up while the economy stagnated or fell", "... and spending still grew",
    "Health priority part above zero", "Size of government part above zero",
    "Economy part above zero", "Countries outside the view (economy -8 to +10, priority -12 to +12)"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(win),
    sum(econ > 0 & prio >= 0),
    sum(econ > 0 & prio < 0),
    sum(econ <= 0 & prio >= 0),
    sum(econ <= 0 & prio < 0),
    sum(lost & total > 0),
    sum(lost & total < 0),
    sum(econ <= 0 & prio > 0),
    sum(econ <= 0 & prio > 0 & total > 0),
    sum(prio > 0),
    sum(win$budget > 0),
    sum(econ > 0),
    sum(econ < -8 | econ > 10 | prio < -12 | prio > 12)
  )
)
lost_table <- tibble(
  `Income group` = unname(INC_LABEL),
  Countries = unname(lost_count),
  Names = unname(lost_names)
)
tables <- list(
  "Counts on the slide" = counts,
  "Countries where health lost priority while the economy grew, by income group" = lost_table
)
show_tables(tables)

# the countries inside the chart's view
points <- win |>
  filter(econ >= -8, econ <= 10, priority >= -12, priority <= 12) |>
  mutate(lost = if_else(lost_priority %in% TRUE,
    "Health lost priority while the economy grew", "Other countries"
  ))
ggplot(points, aes(econ, priority)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = 10, ymin = -12, ymax = 0, fill = "#f6e0da") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = WB[["slate"]], linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = WB[["slate"]], linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = lost), size = 2, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    "Health lost priority while the economy grew" = WB[["rust"]], "Other countries" = WB[["grey"]]
  )) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(-8, 10), breaks = c(-8, -4, 0, 4, 8),
    labels = scales::label_number(style_positive = "plus"), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(-12, 12), breaks = seq(-12, 12, 4),
    labels = scales::label_number(style_positive = "plus"), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Economy part, log points a year", y = "Health priority part, log points a year",
    title = paste(nrow(win), "countries, latest ten-year window")
  )
```

## Slide 9. Health's share of government spending, 2000 to 2023

*Question on the slide: Did the pandemic rise in health's budget share hold?*

We follow the median share of government spending that goes to health in each income group from 2000 to 2023,
with the world median dashed and the pandemic years 2020 and 2021 shaded. Each median is taken over the group's
countries with data in that year. The tables follow the same countries through 2019, 2021 and 2023 and sort the countries into
five paths: rose and kept rising; rose, partly reversed, but still above 2019; rose, then fell back to or below 2019;
did not rise by 2021 but stood above 2019 by 2023; and did not rise, at or below 2019 in 2023. "Kept part of the rise"
counts the first two paths.

Our data stop in 2023. Whether the remaining rise is a lasting change in priorities or a slow withdrawal of pandemic
spending needs later years.

```{r slide-09-health-share, results = "asis"}
## Slide 9: the median share of government spending for health by income group, 2000-2023, and the
## five paths from 2019 to 2023 for the countries with data in 2019, 2021 and 2023.
STATES <- c(
  "Rose and kept rising", "Rose, partly reversed, still above 2019",
  "Rose, then fell back to or below 2019", "Did not rise by 2021, above 2019 by 2023",
  "Did not rise, at or below 2019 in 2023"
)
keys <- c(INC, "world")
pandemic_rows <- mine$pand_grp |>
  filter(key %in% keys) |>
  arrange(match(key, keys))
world_pandemic <- filter(mine$pand_grp, key == "world")

# the median share in 2000, 2019 and 2023, one column per year
shares <- mine$trend |>
  filter(key %in% keys, year %in% c(2000, 2019, 2023)) |>
  select(key, year, med_slice) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = med_slice, names_prefix = "share_") |>
  arrange(match(key, keys))
path_counts <- table(factor(mine$pand$state, levels = STATES))

world_table <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Countries", "Median share, 2019", "Median share, 2021", "Median share, 2023", "Rose by 2021",
    "Above 2019 in 2023"
  ),
  Value = c(
    world_pandemic$n,
    share_pct(world_pandemic$med19),
    share_pct(world_pandemic$med21),
    share_pct(world_pandemic$med23),
    world_pandemic$rose,
    world_pandemic$above19_in23
  )
)
paths_table <- tibble(
  Path = STATES,
  Countries = as.vector(path_counts)
)
group_table <- tibble(
  Group = c(unname(INC_LABEL), "World"),
  `2000` = share_pct(shares$share_2000),
  `2019` = share_pct(shares$share_2019),
  `2023` = share_pct(shares$share_2023),
  `Kept part of the rise` = paste(pandemic_rows$kept, "of", pandemic_rows$n),
  `Median change 2019-2021, points` = signed(pandemic_rows$med_d1921),
  `Median change 2021-2023, points` = signed(pandemic_rows$med_d2123)
)
tables <- list(
  "World, the same countries in 2019, 2021 and 2023" = world_table,
  "Paths from 2019 to 2023 (countries)" = paths_table,
  "Median share of government spending for health, by income group" = group_table
)
show_tables(tables)

line_order <- c("High income", "Upper middle income", "Lower middle income", "Low income", "World")
share_lines <- mine$trend |>
  filter(key %in% keys) |>
  mutate(
    group = if_else(key == "world", "World", INC_LABEL[key]),
    group = factor(group, levels = line_order)
  )
line_ends <- share_lines |>
  filter(year == 2023) |>
  mutate(
    group_short = sub(" income", "", group),
    label = paste0(group_short, " ", share_pct(med_slice))
  )
ggplot(share_lines, aes(year, med_slice, colour = group, linetype = group)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 2019.5, xmax = 2021.5, ymin = 0, ymax = 16, fill = WB[["tint"]]) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_text(
    data = line_ends, aes(x = 2023.4, label = label),
    hjust = 0, size = 3.2, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    "High income" = WB[["navy"]], "Upper middle income" = WB[["blue"]],
    "Lower middle income" = WB[["sky"]], "Low income" = WB[["slate"]], World = WB[["grey"]]
  )) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(
    "High income" = "solid", "Upper middle income" = "solid", "Lower middle income" = "solid",
    "Low income" = "solid", World = "dashed"
  )) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2019, 2023), expand = expansion(add = c(0.3, 5.5))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 16), breaks = seq(0, 16, 4), labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Health, % of government expenditure (median)",
    title = "Median share by income group, 2000-2023", subtitle = "Shaded: 2020 to 2021"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Slide 10. Instructive examples within income groups, latest ten-year window

*Question on the slide: Which countries grew fast through the budget, and kept growing?*

We select examples using a rule applied within each income group over the latest window. A country qualifies if its total growth is at or above its group's 75th percentile, the size of government and health priority together account for at least half of that growth, spending per person grew in both halves (start to middle year, then middle year to end), and its series carries no data flag. The first table gives the thresholds; the second gives the three parts, total and two halves for each example. The slide's halves column uses the most common pair of half-windows, while a country with different halves has its own years after its name.

We use the list as a starting point for reading budget records, not a ranking of policy. Fast growth from a low base is common
among the examples, and the reasons behind each record lie in budget documents that this decomposition does not see.

```{r slide-10-examples, results = "asis", fig.height = 6.4}
## Slide 10: the instructive examples (thresholds by income group, the three
## parts, the total and the two halves).
win <- mine$win |>
  filter(!is.na(total)) |>
  left_join(short_names, by = "iso3")

# the 75th percentile of total growth in each income group, and the examples it gives
thresholds <- win |>
  group_by(income_group) |>
  summarise(
    threshold = quantile(total, 0.75, names = FALSE),
    examples = sum(example %in% TRUE)
  ) |>
  arrange(match(income_group, INC))
examples <- win |>
  filter(example %in% TRUE) |>
  arrange(match(income_group, INC), desc(total))

# The two halves of each window, such as "2013-18 / 2018-23". We print the most common pair once, in
# the third table, and any other pair after the country's name.
halves <- paste0(
  examples$y0, "-", substr(examples$mid, 3, 4), " / ", examples$mid, "-", substr(examples$y1, 3, 4)
)
halves_in_order <- factor(halves, levels = unique(halves))
halves_count <- table(halves_in_order)
common <- names(which.max(halves_count))
other_halves <- if_else(halves != common, paste0(" (", halves, ")"), "")
example_label <- paste0(examples$short, other_halves)
nepal <- filter(examples, iso3 == "NPL")
nepal_range <- paste(dollars(nepal$ghe0), "to", dollars(nepal$ghe1))

threshold_table <- tibble(
  `Income group` = unname(INC_LABEL),
  `75th percentile of total growth` = one_decimal(thresholds$threshold),
  Examples = thresholds$examples
)
example_table <- tibble(
  `Income group` = unname(INC_LABEL[examples$income_group]),
  Country = example_label,
  Economy = signed(examples$econ),
  `Size of government` = signed(examples$budget),
  `Health priority` = signed(examples$priority),
  Total = signed(examples$total),
  `By half of the window` = paste(signed(examples$half1), "/", signed(examples$half2))
)
also_printed <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Examples in all", "Most common half-windows",
    "Nepal, spending per person at the start and end of its window"
  ),
  Value = c(nrow(examples), common, nepal_range)
)
tables <- list(
  "The rule's thresholds and the count of examples by income group" = threshold_table,
  "Instructive examples, log points a year" = example_table,
  "Also printed on the slide" = also_printed
)
show_tables(tables)

# one panel per income group, named without the word "income"
income_panel <- sub(" income", "", INC_LABEL)
bars <- tibble(
  label = example_label,
  econ = examples$econ,
  budget = examples$budget,
  priority = examples$priority,
  total = examples$total,
  group = factor(income_panel[examples$income_group], levels = income_panel)
)
plot_parts(bars, "label", xlab = "Log points a year", facet = "group") +
  labs(title = "The three parts and the total, instructive examples")
```

## Slide 11. Warning cases within income groups, latest ten-year window

*Question on the slide: Where did spending fall, or health lose what growth added?*

We define a country as a warning case if spending per person fell over its window, or if the economy part was positive and health
priority took away at least half of the economy part. The "offset" column
gives the share of the economy part that the fall in priority took away. Countries that meet the rule but carry a data
flag are listed apart in the third table with their flag letters (B break, S shock, E extreme end year, L very low
level), because a flagged series can produce a decline or an offset that is an artefact of the accounts. A window
other than 2013-2023 is shown after the country's name.

We can easily miss the offsets, because spending per person still rose in every one of them: health's falling share does
not show in the total.

```{r slide-11-warnings, results = "asis", fig.height = 9}
## Slide 11: the warning cases without a data flag (declines and priority offsets), and the
## flagged countries that meet the rule.
win <- mine$win |>
  filter(!is.na(total)) |>
  left_join(short_names, by = "iso3")

# A window other than 2013-2023 goes after the country's name. The offset is the share of the
# economy part that the fall in priority took away.
warn <- win |>
  filter(warning %in% TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    reason = if_else(total < 0, "Decline", "Offset"),
    other_window = if_else(y0 != 2013 | y1 != 2023, paste0(" (", y0, " to ", y1, ")"), ""),
    label = paste0(short, other_window)
  ) |>
  arrange(match(income_group, INC), reason != "Decline", total)
warn_table <- warn |>
  transmute(
    reason,
    Country = label,
    Inc. = unname(INC_CODE[income_group]),
    Economy = signed(econ),
    `Size of government` = signed(budget),
    `Health priority` = signed(priority),
    Total = signed(total),
    Offset = paste0(round(100 * -priority / econ), "%")
  )
declines <- warn_table |>
  filter(reason == "Decline") |>
  select(-reason, -Offset)
offsets <- warn_table |>
  filter(reason == "Offset") |>
  select(-reason)

# the countries that meet the rule but carry a data flag
flagged <- win |>
  filter(warning_rule %in% TRUE, !is.na(flag), nzchar(flag)) |>
  arrange(match(income_group, INC), total)

flagged_table <- tibble(
  `Income group` = unname(INC_LABEL[flagged$income_group]),
  Country = paste0(flagged$short, " (", flagged$flag, ")")
)
counts <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Warning cases without a flag", "Declines", "Offsets", "Flagged, listed apart",
    "Lower middle income: declines", "Lower middle income: offsets"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(warn),
    nrow(declines),
    nrow(offsets),
    nrow(flagged),
    sum(warn$reason == "Decline" & warn$income_group == "lower_middle"),
    sum(warn$reason == "Offset" & warn$income_group == "lower_middle")
  )
)
tables <- list(
  "Spending per person fell" = declines,
  "Health priority offset at least half of the economy part" = offsets,
  "Meet the rule but carry a data flag" = flagged_table,
  "Counts on the slide" = counts
)
show_tables(tables)

panel_names <- c(
  Decline = "Spending per person fell",
  Offset = "Health priority offset the economy"
)
bars <- tibble(
  label = warn$label,
  econ = warn$econ,
  budget = warn$budget,
  priority = warn$priority,
  total = warn$total,
  group = factor(panel_names[warn$reason], levels = panel_names)
)
plot_parts(bars, "label", xlab = "Log points a year", facet = "group") +
  labs(title = "The three parts and the total, warning cases without a data flag")
```

## Slide 12. Limits of the decomposition

*Question on the slide: What can this decomposition not tell us?*

On the last slide of Section 1, we place the cautionary evidence alongside the limits. The bar chart shows the share of countries in each income group whose window carries at least one data flag; the second table counts each flag rule (a country can carry more than one). The slide also lists windows ending in 2024, a year GHED releases in stages, the one country without a window and the weight of the largest member in each income group.

We set out five limits on interpretation. The split is an identity, so the parts move together: a fall in GDP raises the government share of GDP on its own. The real-terms conversion mixes prices and exchange rates, so high inflation can distort the economy part. Reclassifications change the shares, while domestic spending excludes external grants that pass through the budget. Part medians do not add up, and group totals reflect their largest members. The rules for examples, warnings and flags are explicit choices that can be changed.

```{r slide-12-limits, results = "asis", fig.height = 3.6}
## Slide 12: data flags by income group and by rule, windows ending in 2024, countries without a
## window, and the largest member of each income group.
win <- mine$win |>
  filter(!is.na(total)) |>
  mutate(any_flag = !is.na(flag) & nzchar(flag))
flags_by_income <- win |>
  group_by(income_group) |>
  summarise(countries = n(), flagged = sum(any_flag)) |>
  arrange(match(income_group, INC))

# the largest member of each income group and its share of the group's spending in 2023
largest <- mine$contrib |>
  filter(income_group %in% INC) |>
  group_by(income_group) |>
  mutate(share = 100 * ghe1_musd / sum(ghe1_musd)) |>
  slice_max(ghe1_musd, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(match(income_group, INC)) |>
  left_join(short_names, by = "iso3") |>
  transmute(
    `Income group` = unname(INC_LABEL[income_group]),
    `Largest member` = short,
    `Share of the group's spending, 2023` = whole_pct(share)
  )

# windows ending in 2024 and countries without a window, by their full names
names_2024 <- win$name[win$note_2024 %in% TRUE]
names_without_window <- mine$win$name[is.na(mine$win$total)]

flag_table <- tibble(
  `Income group` = unname(INC_LABEL),
  Flagged = flags_by_income$flagged,
  Countries = flags_by_income$countries,
  Share = whole_pct(100 * flags_by_income$flagged / flags_by_income$countries)
)
rule_table <- tibble(
  Flag = c("B", "S", "E", "L", "Any"),
  Rule = c(
    "Break: a budget share doubles or halves in one year",
    "Shock: real GDP per person up 25% or down 20% in one year",
    "Extreme end: a share at either end over twice or under half its window median",
    "Level: government spending over 100% of GDP, or health spending under US$1 a person",
    "At least one flag"
  ),
  Countries = c(
    sum(grepl("B", win$flag)), sum(grepl("S", win$flag)), sum(grepl("E", win$flag)),
    sum(grepl("L", win$flag)), sum(win$any_flag)
  )
)
window_table <- tibble(
  Item = c("Countries with a window", "Windows ending in 2024", "No window"),
  Value = c(
    nrow(win),
    knitr::combine_words(names_2024, oxford_comma = FALSE),
    knitr::combine_words(names_without_window, oxford_comma = FALSE)
  )
)
tables <- list(
  "Countries whose window carries a data flag, by income group" = flag_table,
  "Flag rules, inside each country's window" = rule_table,
  "Windows and members" = window_table,
  "Largest member of each income group" = largest
)
show_tables(tables)

flag_share <- tibble(
  group = factor(INC_LABEL, levels = rev(INC_LABEL)),
  pct = 100 * flags_by_income$flagged / flags_by_income$countries,
  label = paste(flags_by_income$flagged, "of", flags_by_income$countries)
)
ggplot(flag_share, aes(x = pct, y = group)) +
  geom_col(fill = WB[["rust"]], width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), hjust = -0.1, size = 3.3) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 55), breaks = c(0, 25, 50), labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Countries whose window carries a data flag", y = NULL,
    title = "Data flags by income group, latest window"
  )
```

# Section 2. The 2027-2029 health budget prescription

## Slide 13. How much should the health budget ask for, 2027 to 2029?

*Kicker on the slide: Section 2.*

On the divider, we open Section 2 with its subtitle, "The least to ask for, the most to ask for, and the room growth leaves",
and list the titles of the eight slides that follow. The numbers behind those slides come from the prescription engine
described above, so no computation sits here.

## Slide 14. The method in one country: Kenya, 2024 to 2029

*Question on the slide: How much should the health budget ask for?*

We use Kenya to show the method on one country, in billions of Kenyan shillings at current prices. The top panel is GDP from the
IMF; the middle panel is government spending on the IMF path, with the flat-share path dotted; the bottom panel is the
health budget. The growth of government spending above its 2026 level is the ceiling. Holding health's 2026 share
(*h*, the value at the end of Kenya's window, held to 2026) on that growth gives the protect amount, the least to ask for. The upper
ask is the largest admissible candidate; in Kenya the own trend in health's share is positive but smaller than the
+0.75-point step, so the step sets the ask.

From 2026 on, we use IMF projections, and *h* itself is a nowcast for 2025 and 2026. The amounts here are nominal;
the real versions, and the conversion to US\$, come on the next slides.

```{r slide-14-kenya, results = "asis", fig.height = 6.6}
## Slide 14: Kenya, the method drawn from 2024 to 2029 (GDP, government spending on both paths, the
## health budget at the protect amount and on the upper-ask path), KES billion at current prices.
kenya_lines <- mine$rx_lines |>
  filter(iso3 == "KEN") |>
  arrange(year)
kenya_imf <- filter(kenya_lines, variant == "imf")
kenya_flat <- filter(kenya_lines, variant == "flat")
kenya <- mine$rx |>
  filter(iso3 == "KEN", variant == "imf") |>
  arrange(year) # 2027, 2028 and 2029
kenya_2029 <- filter(kenya, year == 2029)
imf_2029 <- filter(kenya_imf, year == 2029)
flat_2029 <- filter(kenya_flat, year == 2029)

kenya_table <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Ceiling, 2026 to 2029", "Health's share of government spending, %", "Protect amount, 2029",
    "Upper ask, 2029", "Upper ask, % of the ceiling", "GDP, 2029",
    "Government spending, 2029, IMF path", "Government spending, 2029, flat share",
    "Health budget at the upper ask, 2029", "Health budget at the protect amount, 2029"
  ),
  Value = c(
    one_decimal(kenya_2029$d_all / 1e9),
    one_decimal(kenya_2029$h),
    one_decimal(kenya_2029$d_protect / 1e9),
    one_decimal(kenya_2029$ask / 1e9),
    whole_pct(kenya_2029$ask_share_of_ceiling_nominal),
    one_decimal(imf_2029$gdp / 1e9),
    one_decimal(imf_2029$gge / 1e9),
    one_decimal(flat_2029$gge / 1e9),
    one_decimal((kenya_2029$health26 + kenya_2029$ask) / 1e9),
    one_decimal(imf_2029$health_protect / 1e9)
  )
)
tables <- list("Kenya, KES billion at current prices, IMF path" = kenya_table)
show_tables(tables)

# Three panels: GDP, government spending on both paths, and the health budget at the
# protect amount and on the upper-ask path
upper_ask <- tibble(
  year = 2026:2029,
  v = c(kenya_2029$health26, kenya$health26 + kenya$ask)
)
flat_from_2026 <- filter(kenya_flat, year >= 2026)
line_names <- c(
  "IMF path", "Flat spending share", "Protect: health's share held",
  "Upper ask: +0.75 points a year"
)
kenya_long <- bind_rows(
  tibble(panel = "A. GDP", year = kenya_imf$year, v = kenya_imf$gdp / 1e9, line = line_names[1]),
  tibble(
    panel = "B. Government spending", year = kenya_imf$year, v = kenya_imf$gge / 1e9,
    line = line_names[1]
  ),
  tibble(
    panel = "B. Government spending", year = flat_from_2026$year, v = flat_from_2026$gge / 1e9,
    line = line_names[2]
  ),
  tibble(
    panel = "C. Health budget", year = kenya_imf$year, v = kenya_imf$health_protect / 1e9,
    line = line_names[3]
  ),
  tibble(
    panel = "C. Health budget", year = upper_ask$year, v = upper_ask$v / 1e9,
    line = line_names[4]
  )
) |>
  mutate(line = factor(line, levels = line_names))
ggplot(kenya_long, aes(year, v, colour = line, linetype = line)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 2026, xmax = 2029, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#f2f4f6") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = setNames(c(WB[["blue"]], WB[["grey"]], WB[["rust"]], WB[["navy"]]), line_names)
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames(c("solid", "dotted", "solid", "dashed"), line_names)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2024:2029) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "KES billion, current prices",
    title = "Kenya: the ceiling, the protect amount and the upper ask",
    caption = "Shaded years: IMF projections from 2026."
  )
```

## Slide 15. Protect amount, upper ask and ceiling by income group, 2029

*Question on the slide: How much room does growth leave, and how much must health ask for?*

We compare the median country's protect amount, upper ask and ceiling for 2029 on the IMF path, in real terms, across income groups. The chart shows each real increase over 2026 as a per cent of the 2026 health budget, using a log scale because the ceiling is many times the protect amount. The table gives the same medians in constant 2026 US\$ per person. Each median is calculated separately, and the upper ask includes only countries where the method applies.

The ceiling equals the protect amount divided by health's share, so a country spending 5% of its budget on health has a
ceiling twenty times its protect amount, and one spending 15% about seven times. The ratio explains why the ceiling is very large in
per cent where health's share is small, while the dollar amounts per person stay small in low-income countries.

```{r slide-15-groups, results = "asis", fig.height = 4.4}
## Slide 15: median protect amount, upper ask and ceiling in 2029 (IMF path, real), by
## income group, in per cent of the 2026 health budget and in constant 2026 US$ per person;
## and the regional values the slide quotes.
groups_2029 <- filter(mine$rx_grp, variant == "imf", year == 2029)
income_2029 <- groups_2029 |>
  filter(key %in% c("world", INC)) |>
  arrange(match(key, c("world", INC)))
group_names <- c("World", unname(INC_LABEL))
south_asia <- filter(groups_2029, key == "South Asia")
africa <- filter(groups_2029, key == "Sub-Saharan Africa")

median_table <- tibble(
  Group = group_names,
  n = income_2029$n,
  `Protect, %` = share_pct(income_2029$med_d_protect_pct),
  `Upper ask, %` = share_pct(income_2029$med_ask_pct),
  `Ceiling, %` = whole_pct(income_2029$med_d_all_pct),
  `Protect, US$ per person` = dollars(income_2029$med_d_protect_usd_pp),
  `Upper ask, US$ per person` = dollars(income_2029$med_ask_usd_pp),
  `Ceiling, US$ per person` = dollars(income_2029$med_d_all_usd_pp),
  `Upper ask, % of the real ceiling` = whole_pct(income_2029$med_ask_share_of_ceiling)
)
also_printed <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Ceiling as a multiple of the protect amount at a 15% share", "South Asia: ceiling",
    "Sub-Saharan Africa: ceiling", "Sub-Saharan Africa: upper ask",
    "Sub-Saharan Africa: upper ask per person"
  ),
  Value = c(
    round(100 / 15),
    whole_pct(south_asia$med_d_all_pct),
    whole_pct(africa$med_d_all_pct),
    share_pct(africa$med_ask_pct),
    dollars(africa$med_ask_usd_pp)
  )
)
tables <- list(
  "Median country, 2029, IMF path, real increase over 2026" = median_table,
  "Also printed on the slide" = also_printed
)
show_tables(tables)

# a dot for each amount on a log scale, joined from the protect amount to the ceiling
amount_names <- c("Protect, the minimum ask", "Upper ask", "Ceiling")
dots <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    group = group_names, v = income_2029$med_d_protect_pct, what = amount_names[1],
    label = share_pct(income_2029$med_d_protect_pct)
  ),
  tibble(
    group = group_names, v = income_2029$med_ask_pct, what = amount_names[2],
    label = share_pct(income_2029$med_ask_pct)
  ),
  tibble(
    group = group_names, v = income_2029$med_d_all_pct, what = amount_names[3],
    label = whole_pct(income_2029$med_d_all_pct)
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    group = factor(group, levels = rev(group_names)),
    what = factor(what, levels = amount_names)
  )
ranges <- tibble(
  group = factor(group_names, levels = rev(group_names)),
  from = income_2029$med_d_protect_pct,
  to = income_2029$med_d_all_pct
)
ggplot(dots, aes(x = v, y = group)) +
  geom_segment(
    data = ranges, aes(x = from, xend = to, y = group, yend = group),
    colour = WB[["grey"]], linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = what, fill = what), size = 3.6, colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = label, colour = what), vjust = -1.1, size = 3.1, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_log10(
    limits = c(1, 500), breaks = c(1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500),
    labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1)
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(22, 21, 23)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(c("#8f99a3", WB[["blue"]], WB[["navy"]]), amount_names)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c("black", WB[["blue"]], "black"), amount_names)) +
  labs(
    x = "Real increase 2026 to 2029, % of the 2026 health budget (log scale)", y = NULL,
    title = "Median country, IMF path, 2026 prices"
  )
```

## Slide 16. Where the method does not apply, 2027 to 2029

*Question on the slide: Where is the budget itself the question?*

Our method needs a growing government budget. Where government spending in national currency is lower than in 2026, the
method does not apply and the question becomes the fiscal envelope rather than health's priority. The first table counts
those countries by year on each path, the countries where the budget grows in currency but falls in real terms, and the
countries where the real upper ask is larger than the real growth of the whole budget. The second table lists every
country in which government spending does not grow in at least one year.

On the IMF path, we find that most cases where the method does not apply come from a falling projected spending share, a fiscal stance, rather than from a
shrinking economy: with the share held flat, only three countries remain, those where nominal GDP itself falls.

```{r slide-16-not-apply, results = "asis", fig.height = 4}
## Slide 16: countries where the method does not apply (government spending does not grow), where
## the budget falls in real terms only, and where the upper ask exceeds real budget growth; and the
## list of countries without budget growth.
world_rx <- filter(mine$rx_grp, key == "world")
world_imf <- world_rx |>
  filter(variant == "imf") |>
  arrange(year)
world_flat <- world_rx |>
  filter(variant == "flat") |>
  arrange(year)

# Every country with IMF projections in which government spending does not grow in at least one
# year, on either path. The deck's builder sorts these names by code point, as arrange() does.
with_projections <- filter(mine$rx, has_data %in% TRUE)
no_growth <- with_projections |>
  filter(!(applies %in% TRUE)) |>
  arrange(year) |>
  group_by(iso3, name, income_group) |>
  summarise(
    imf = paste(year[variant == "imf"], collapse = ", "),
    flat = paste(year[variant == "flat"], collapse = ", "),
    n_imf = sum(variant == "imf"),
    n_flat = sum(variant == "flat"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    imf = if_else(n_imf > 0, imf, "-"),
    flat = if_else(n_flat > 0, flat, "-")
  ) |>
  arrange(name) |>
  left_join(short_names, by = "iso3")
ask_above <- with_projections |>
  filter(variant == "imf", ask_above_real_ceiling %in% TRUE) |>
  distinct(iso3) |>
  nrow()
flat_names <- no_growth$name[no_growth$n_flat > 0]

by_year <- tibble(
  Year = 2027:2029,
  `Does not apply, IMF path` = world_imf$n_not_applies,
  `Falls in real terms only, IMF path` = world_imf$n_real_fall_only,
  `Does not apply, flat share` = world_flat$n_not_applies,
  `Upper ask above real budget growth, IMF path` = world_imf$n_ask_above_real_ceiling,
  `Countries with IMF projections` = world_imf$n
)
across_years <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Does not apply in at least one year, IMF path", "Does not apply, flat share",
    "Upper ask above real budget growth in at least one year, IMF path"
  ),
  Value = c(
    sum(no_growth$n_imf > 0),
    knitr::combine_words(flat_names, oxford_comma = FALSE),
    ask_above
  )
)
no_growth_table <- tibble(
  Country = no_growth$short,
  Inc. = unname(INC_CODE[no_growth$income_group]),
  `IMF path` = no_growth$imf,
  `Flat share` = no_growth$flat
)
tables <- list(
  "Countries by year" = by_year,
  "Counts across the three years" = across_years,
  "Years in which government spending does not grow" = no_growth_table
)
show_tables(tables)

series <- c(
  "Does not apply, IMF path", "Falls in real terms only, IMF path", "Does not apply, flat share"
)
counts_by_year <- tibble(
  year = factor(rep(2027:2029, 3), levels = 2029:2027),
  series = factor(rep(series, each = 3), levels = rev(series)),
  v = c(world_imf$n_not_applies, world_imf$n_real_fall_only, world_flat$n_not_applies)
)
ggplot(counts_by_year, aes(x = v, y = year, fill = series)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(aes(label = v), position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), hjust = -0.3, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = setNames(c(WB[["rust"]], WB[["rosy"]], "#8f99a3"), series),
    breaks = series
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 35), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    x = paste("Countries, of", world_imf$n[world_imf$year == 2029], "with IMF projections"),
    y = NULL, title = "Countries by year"
  )
```

## Slide 17. The upper ask: own trend against the fixed steps, 2027 to 2029

*Question on the slide: What sets the upper ask: the country's own trend or a fixed step?*

We define the upper ask as the largest admissible candidate: the country's own trend in health's share (if the share rose over the
window) or a fixed step of +0.25, +0.5 or +0.75 points a year. The chart and the first table count which candidate set
the ask in each year, among the countries where the method applies. The second table sorts every country's own trend
into bands, by income group: the trend is the change in health's share over the window divided by the window's length,
in percentage points a year.

We find that health's share rose by more than 0.75 points a year in only one country over the last decade, so the +0.75 step sets the
ask almost everywhere and the upper ask behaves close to a fixed rule. The same step is a larger relative rise where
health's share is low.

```{r slide-17-setter, results = "asis", fig.height = 3.4}
## Slide 17: which candidate set the upper ask in each year (IMF path), the own trend in health's
## share by band and income group, and the upper ask as a share of the real ceiling.
SETTERS <- c(
  "075" = "+0.75 a year", "050" = "+0.5 a year", "025" = "+0.25 a year", trend = "Own trend",
  none = "None admissible"
)
world_imf <- mine$rx_grp |>
  filter(key == "world", variant == "imf") |>
  arrange(year)
groups_2029 <- filter(mine$rx_grp, variant == "imf", year == 2029)

# the own trend in health's share is the same in every year, so one
# year (2027) gives one row per country
rows_2027 <- filter(mine$rx, variant == "imf", year == 2027)
trends <- rows_2027$trend[!is.na(rows_2027$trend)]
trend_rows <- bind_rows(
  mutate(rows_2027, Countries = "World"),
  mutate(rows_2027, Countries = unname(INC_LABEL[income_group]))
)
bands <- trend_rows |>
  filter(!is.na(trend)) |>
  group_by(Countries) |>
  summarise(
    `Fell or flat` = sum(trend <= 0),
    `Up to 0.25` = sum(trend > 0 & trend <= 0.25),
    `0.25 to 0.5` = sum(trend > 0.25 & trend <= 0.5),
    `0.5 to 0.75` = sum(trend > 0.5 & trend <= 0.75),
    `Above 0.75` = sum(trend > 0.75),
    n = n()
  ) |>
  arrange(match(Countries, c("World", INC_LABEL)))

setter_table <- tibble(
  Year = 2027:2029,
  `+0.75 a year` = world_imf$set_075,
  `+0.5 a year` = world_imf$set_050,
  `+0.25 a year` = world_imf$set_025,
  `Own trend` = world_imf$set_trend,
  `None admissible` = world_imf$set_none,
  `Method applies` = world_imf$n_applies
)
also_printed <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Median trend, points a year", "Middle half, from", "Middle half, to",
    "Upper ask, % of the real ceiling, 2029: world", "low income", "high income"
  ),
  Value = c(
    signed(median(trends)),
    one_decimal(quantile(trends, 0.25, names = FALSE)),
    signed(quantile(trends, 0.75, names = FALSE)),
    whole_pct(world_imf$med_ask_share_of_ceiling[world_imf$year == 2029]),
    whole_pct(groups_2029$med_ask_share_of_ceiling[groups_2029$key == "low"]),
    whole_pct(groups_2029$med_ask_share_of_ceiling[groups_2029$key == "high"])
  )
)
tables <- list(
  "Candidate that set the upper ask, IMF path (countries where the method applies)" = setter_table,
  "Own trend in health's share, points a year, latest decade" = bands,
  "Also printed on the slide" = also_printed
)
show_tables(tables)

# the count of each candidate in each year, as a share of the countries where the method applies
set_by <- world_imf |>
  select(
    year,
    total = n_applies, `075` = set_075, `050` = set_050, `025` = set_025, trend = set_trend,
    none = set_none
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(year, total), names_to = "setter", values_to = "n") |>
  mutate(
    year = factor(year, levels = 2029:2027),
    setter = factor(SETTERS[setter], levels = rev(SETTERS)),
    # we write the count on segments of five countries or more
    label = if_else(n >= 5, as.character(n), "")
  )
ggplot(set_by, aes(x = 100 * n / total, y = year, fill = setter)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label, group = setter),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), colour = "white", size = 3.2
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = setNames(
      c(WB[["navy"]], WB[["blue"]], WB[["light"]], WB[["rust"]], "#d5dade"), unname(SETTERS)
    ),
    breaks = unname(SETTERS)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100), labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.03))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Share of countries where the method applies (labels: countries)", y = NULL,
    title = "Candidate that sets the upper ask, IMF path"
  )
```

## Slide 18. IMF spending path against a flat spending share, 2029

*Question on the slide: Does the IMF's spending path change the answer?*

The IMF path carries the IMF's fiscal assumptions for each country, including consolidation. The flat path holds the
2026 expenditure share of GDP, so government spending grows with GDP. The scatter compares each country's real growth of
government spending from 2026 to 2029 on the two paths; points above the dashed line get more from the flat share. The
table compares the median real ceiling and the median real upper ask on the two paths, by income group.

We find that the ceiling depends heavily on the path and the upper ask less so, since the ask applies a share to the budget while
the ceiling is the whole increase. The path also decides where the method applies at all.

```{r slide-18-paths, results = "asis", fig.height = 5.6}
## Slide 18: the IMF path against a flat spending share in 2029: country by country real growth of
## government spending, the ceiling and the upper ask on each path, and the medians by income group.
with_data <- unique(mine$rx$iso3[mine$rx$has_data %in% TRUE])
imf_2029 <- mine$rx |>
  filter(variant == "imf", year == 2029, iso3 %in% with_data) |>
  select(
    iso3,
    imf_ceiling = d_all_pct, imf_ask = ask_pct, imf_real = d_all_real, imf_gge26 = gge26
  )
flat_2029 <- mine$rx |>
  filter(variant == "flat", year == 2029, iso3 %in% with_data) |>
  select(
    iso3,
    flat_ceiling = d_all_pct, flat_ask = ask_pct, flat_real = d_all_real, flat_gge26 = gge26
  )

# Each country on both paths. The deck rounds the real growth of government spending to one decimal
# before it places a country on the chart, so we do the same.
paths <- inner_join(imf_2029, flat_2029, by = "iso3") |>
  mutate(
    ask_close = !is.na(imf_ask) & !is.na(flat_ask) & abs(flat_ask - imf_ask) < 5,
    imf_growth = round(100 * imf_real / imf_gge26, 1),
    flat_growth = round(100 * flat_real / flat_gge26, 1),
    in_view = imf_growth >= -50 & imf_growth <= 100 & flat_growth >= -50 & flat_growth <= 100
  )

# the medians by group on each path
imf_groups <- mine$rx_grp |>
  filter(variant == "imf", year == 2029, key %in% c("world", INC)) |>
  arrange(match(key, c("world", INC)))
flat_groups <- mine$rx_grp |>
  filter(variant == "flat", year == 2029, key %in% c("world", INC)) |>
  arrange(match(key, c("world", INC)))

country_counts <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Flat share gives a larger ceiling", "Countries",
    "Median difference in the ceiling, points of the 2026 health budget",
    "Upper ask differs by less than 5 points", "Countries outside the chart's view",
    "Does not apply, IMF path", "Does not apply, flat share",
    "Median upper ask per person, IMF path", "Median upper ask per person, flat share"
  ),
  Value = c(
    sum(paths$flat_ceiling > paths$imf_ceiling),
    nrow(paths),
    scales::comma(median(paths$flat_ceiling - paths$imf_ceiling), accuracy = 1),
    sum(paths$ask_close),
    sum(!paths$in_view),
    imf_groups$n_not_applies[1],
    flat_groups$n_not_applies[1],
    dollars(imf_groups$med_ask_usd_pp[1]),
    dollars(flat_groups$med_ask_usd_pp[1])
  )
)
group_medians <- tibble(
  Group = c("World", unname(INC_LABEL)),
  `Ceiling, IMF` = whole_pct(imf_groups$med_d_all_pct),
  `Ceiling, flat` = whole_pct(flat_groups$med_d_all_pct),
  `Ask, IMF` = share_pct(imf_groups$med_ask_pct),
  `Ask, flat` = share_pct(flat_groups$med_ask_pct),
  n = imf_groups$n
)
tables <- list(
  "Countries with IMF projections, 2029" = country_counts,
  "Median real increase, % of the 2026 health budget, 2029" = group_medians
)
show_tables(tables)

in_view <- paths |>
  filter(in_view) |>
  mutate(side = if_else(flat_growth > imf_growth, "Flat share gives more", "IMF path gives more"))
ggplot(in_view, aes(imf_growth, flat_growth)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = WB[["grey"]]) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = WB[["grey"]]) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = side), size = 2, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("Flat share gives more" = WB[["blue"]], "IMF path gives more" = "#8f99a3")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(-50, 100), breaks = seq(-50, 100, 25), labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(-50, 100), breaks = seq(-50, 100, 25), labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    x = "IMF path: real growth of government spending, 2026 to 2029", y = "Flat share: real growth",
    title = "Each country, 2026 prices", caption = "Dashed line: the two paths agree."
  )
```

## Slide 19. Worked examples: Ethiopia, Kenya and Indonesia, 2029

*Question on the slide: What would the prescription ask for in three countries?*

We use three countries to show the method at work in 2029 on the IMF path. For each, the ladder chart expresses the protect amount
and every candidate as a percentage of the real ceiling (ceiling = 100), with the upper ask darkest. The tables give the
amounts behind the ladder: the increase over 2026 in national currency at current prices, in US\$ million at the IMF's
2029 exchange rate, and as a real percentage of the 2026 health budget.

In Ethiopia, we find no trend candidate because its health share fell over the window, and its prices rise fast enough that a
nominal increase shrinks a good deal in real terms. Kenya's own trend is positive but below the step. In Indonesia the
ask is a small share of the nominal ceiling. In all three the +0.75-point step sets the ask.

```{r slide-19-examples, results = "asis", fig.height = 4}
## Slide 19: Ethiopia, Kenya and Indonesia in 2029, IMF path: protect amount, candidates, upper ask
## and ceiling, with the share of the real ceiling each represents.
UNIT <- list(
  ETH = list(div = 1e9, cur = "ETB", scale = "billion", name = "Ethiopia"),
  KEN = list(div = 1e9, cur = "KES", scale = "billion", name = "Kenya"),
  IDN = list(div = 1e12, cur = "IDR", scale = "trillion", name = "Indonesia")
)
CAND <- c(
  protect = "d_protect", trend = "c_trend", s025 = "c_025", s050 = "c_050", s075 = "c_075",
  ask = "ask", ceiling = "d_all"
)
CAND_LABEL <- c(
  protect = "Protect", trend = "Own trend", s025 = "+0.25 a year", s050 = "+0.5 a year",
  s075 = "+0.75 a year", ask = "Upper ask", ceiling = "Ceiling"
)

tables <- list()
ladder <- NULL
for (iso in c("ETH", "KEN", "IDN")) {
  row_2029 <- filter(mine$rx, iso3 == iso, variant == "imf", year == 2029)
  unit <- UNIT[[iso]]
  # Each amount in four units: national currency, US$ million, the real rise in % of the 2026 health
  # budget and % of the real ceiling. The own-trend candidate exists only where health's share rose.
  trend_ok <- !is.na(row_2029$trend) && row_2029$trend > 0
  # The builder rounds US$ million to one decimal and the slide prints it whole in
  # JavaScript, which rounds a half away from zero where R's round() goes to the even
  # number; we round in the same two steps.
  amounts <- tibble(
    key = names(CAND),
    nominal = unlist(row_2029[CAND]),
    usd = unlist(row_2029[paste0(CAND, "_usd")]),
    real_pct = unlist(row_2029[paste0(CAND, "_pct")]),
    real = unlist(row_2029[paste0(CAND, "_real")])
  ) |>
    mutate(
      shown = !is.na(nominal) & (key != "trend" | trend_ok),
      of_ceiling = 100 * real / row_2029$d_all_real,
      usd_tenths = round(usd / 1e6, 1),
      # a half away from zero, as in JavaScript
      usd_whole = sign(usd_tenths) * floor(abs(usd_tenths) + 0.5)
    )
  caption <- paste0(
    unit$name, ", 2029, IMF path: health ", one_decimal(row_2029$h), "% of government spending"
  )
  tables[[caption]] <- amounts |>
    transmute(
      Amount = unname(CAND_LABEL[key]),
      `National currency` = if_else(
        shown, paste(unit$cur, one_decimal(nominal / unit$div), unit$scale), "-"
      ),
      `US$ million` = if_else(shown, scales::comma(usd_whole, accuracy = 1), "-"),
      `Real, % of the 2026 health budget` = if_else(
        shown, signed_pct(real_pct), "-"
      ),
      `% of the real ceiling` = if_else(
        shown & !key %in% c("ask", "ceiling"), one_decimal(of_ceiling), "-"
      )
    )
  # the ladder chart: the protect amount and the candidates as % of the real ceiling
  rungs <- amounts |>
    filter(key %in% c("protect", "trend", "s025", "s050", "s075")) |>
    transmute(
      country = unit$name,
      cand = unname(CAND_LABEL[key]),
      v = if_else(shown, of_ceiling, NA),
      role = case_when(
        key == "protect" ~ "Protect",
        key == row_2029$setter ~ "Upper ask",
        .default = "Other candidate"
      )
    )
  ladder <- bind_rows(ladder, rungs)
}
eth <- filter(mine$rx, iso3 == "ETH", variant == "imf", year == 2029)
ken <- filter(mine$rx, iso3 == "KEN", variant == "imf", year == 2029)
idn <- filter(mine$rx, iso3 == "IDN", variant == "imf", year == 2029)
# Ethiopia's price rise as the slide prints it: the builder keeps the price level to three decimals
# and the slide rounds the per cent half up
eth_price_level <- round(eth$p, 3)
eth_price_rise <- floor(100 * (eth_price_level - 1) + 0.5)
setters <- unique(c(eth$setter_label, ken$setter_label, idn$setter_label))
tables[["Also printed on the slide"]] <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Ethiopia: own trend, points a year", "Ethiopia: price rise 2026 to 2029",
    "Kenya: own trend, points a year", "Kenya: health's share reached by the ask, 2029",
    "Indonesia: ask, % of the nominal ceiling",
    "Indonesia: health's share reached by the ask, 2029",
    "Upper ask set by, all three"
  ),
  Value = c(
    signed(eth$trend),
    paste0(eth_price_rise, "%"),
    signed(ken$trend),
    share_pct(ken$h_ask),
    whole_pct(idn$ask_share_of_ceiling_nominal),
    share_pct(idn$h_ask),
    paste(setters, collapse = ", ")
  )
)
show_tables(tables)

rung_names <- unname(CAND_LABEL[c("protect", "trend", "s025", "s050", "s075")])
ladder <- ladder |>
  mutate(
    cand = factor(cand, levels = rev(rung_names)),
    country = factor(country, levels = c("Ethiopia", "Kenya", "Indonesia")),
    bar = coalesce(v, 0),
    label = if_else(is.na(v), "share fell: no candidate", one_decimal(v))
  )
ggplot(ladder, aes(x = bar, y = cand, fill = role)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 100, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~country) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(Protect = "#8f99a3", "Upper ask" = WB[["navy"]], "Other candidate" = WB[["light"]]),
    breaks = c("Protect", "Other candidate", "Upper ask")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 115), breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    x = "% of the real ceiling (ceiling = 100)", y = NULL,
    title = "Protect amount and candidates, 2029, IMF path"
  )
```

## Slide 20. The policy table: Ethiopia, Kenya and Indonesia, 2027 to 2029

*Question on the slide: What would the prescription ask for in three countries?*

We use the policy table to lay out every amount the method produces for the three countries in each year from 2027 to 2029, on
the IMF path: the protect amount, each candidate, the upper ask with the candidate that sets it, and the ceiling. Each
cell gives the increase over 2026 in national currency at current prices, then its real rise as a percentage of the
2026 health budget and its value in US\$ million at that year's IMF exchange rate. A dash in the own-trend column means
the country's health share fell over its window, so there is no trend candidate.

Because the slide is itself a table, we print the table in this chunk and draw no separate figure. Nominal amounts include
inflation, and the real percentage in each cell shows how much of each increase is left at 2026 prices.

```{r slide-20-policy-table, results = "asis"}
## Slide 20: the policy table for Ethiopia, Kenya and Indonesia, 2027 to
## 2029, IMF path; one table per country.
tables <- list()
for (iso in c("ETH", "KEN", "IDN")) {
  unit <- UNIT[[iso]]
  country_years <- mine$rx |>
    filter(iso3 == iso, variant == "imf") |>
    arrange(year)
  policy_rows <- NULL
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(country_years))) {
    one_year <- country_years[i, ]
    # the amounts as on slide 19: the nominal increase, then (the real rise in %, US$ million)
    trend_ok <- !is.na(one_year$trend) && one_year$trend > 0
    nominal <- unlist(one_year[CAND])
    real_pct <- unlist(one_year[paste0(CAND, "_pct")])
    usd <- unlist(one_year[paste0(CAND, "_usd")])
    shown <- !is.na(nominal) & (names(CAND) != "trend" | trend_ok)
    national <- one_decimal(nominal / unit$div)
    real_rise <- signed_pct(real_pct)
    # US$ million rounded in two steps, as on slide 19
    usd_tenths <- round(usd / 1e6, 1)
    # a half away from zero, as in JavaScript
    usd_whole <- sign(usd_tenths) * floor(abs(usd_tenths) + 0.5)
    usd_million <- scales::comma(usd_whole, accuracy = 1)
    cell <- if_else(shown, paste0(national, " (", real_rise, ", US$", usd_million, " m)"), "-")
    policy_rows <- bind_rows(policy_rows, tibble(
      Year = as.character(one_year$year),
      Protect = cell[1],
      `Own trend` = cell[2],
      `+0.25 a year` = cell[3],
      `+0.5 a year` = cell[4],
      `+0.75 a year` = cell[5],
      `Upper ask` = cell[6],
      `Set by` = sub(" a year", "", one_year$setter_label),
      Ceiling = cell[7]
    ))
  }
  first_year <- country_years[1, ]
  caption <- paste0(
    unit$name, ": ", unit$cur, " ", unit$scale, "; health ", one_decimal(first_year$h),
    "% of government spending; own trend ", signed(first_year$trend), " points a year"
  )
  tables[[caption]] <- policy_rows
}
show_tables(tables)
```

## Slide 21. Limits of the prescription and what each country team checks

*Question on the slide: What can the prescription not tell a country?*

On the last slide of Section 2, we present the prescription as a starting point for budget dialogue. The prescription tests an ask only against the ceiling, so whether the money can be spent, and spent well, is for the country team to judge from budget execution, an investment case, the latest approved budget and its health share, and health prices that may rise faster than the GDP deflator. The slide reports coverage counts and countries without an IMF series. Peer benchmarks by region or income group do not determine the ask.

We set amounts in current prices, the budget unit, and the countries whose 2029 budget grows in currency but falls in
real terms are counted here again. The IMF projections are revised twice a year, and the own trend is a decade's average
that can hide a recent reversal.

```{r slide-21-limits, results = "asis"}
## Slide 21: coverage of the prescription and the countries without an IMF
## series (the slide is text; no figure).
countries_with_base <- unique(mine$rx$iso3)
countries_with_data <- unique(mine$rx$iso3[mine$rx$has_data %in% TRUE])
world_2029 <- filter(mine$rx_grp, key == "world", variant == "imf", year == 2029)

# The countries without an IMF series, sorted by code point as the deck's builder sorts them, and
# printed without the bracket or the east Jerusalem note in their GHED names
no_imf_names <- mine$rx |>
  filter(!iso3 %in% countries_with_data) |>
  distinct(iso3, name) |>
  arrange(name) |>
  mutate(
    name = sub("\\s*\\(.*\\)$", "", name),
    name = sub(", including east Jerusalem$", "", name)
  ) |>
  pull(name)
no_base_names <- countries$name[!countries$iso3 %in% countries_with_base]

coverage <- tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Countries with a Section 1 base", "Countries with IMF projections",
    "2029 budget grows in currency but falls in real terms, IMF path", "No IMF series",
    "No GHED base"
  ),
  Value = c(
    length(countries_with_base),
    length(countries_with_data),
    world_2029$n_real_fall_only,
    knitr::combine_words(no_imf_names, oxford_comma = FALSE),
    knitr::combine_words(no_base_names, oxford_comma = FALSE)
  )
)
tables <- list("Coverage" = coverage)
show_tables(tables)
```

# Annex A. Every country's decomposition, by World Bank region

Across the seven annex A slides, we list every country with its latest window, grouped by World Bank region: government health
spending per person in the window's last year (constant 2023 US\$), the total change and its three parts in log points a
year, the pattern (with an asterisk where health lost priority while the economy grew) and any data flag. Two regions
are long enough to be split over two slides, alphabetically. Each slide gets its own chunk, built from one function, and
prints the slide's table and the region line in its lead (the pattern counts and, for regions with at least eight
countries, the median country's total). The slides are tables, so no figure is drawn. Inc.: Low, LM lower middle, UM
upper middle, High; flags: B break, S shock, E extreme end, L level.

```{r annex-helpers}
## The seven slides shared by annexes A and B (which countries each
## slide lists), and the annex A table.
annex_slides <- tibble(
  slide = 1:7,
  lead_region = c(
    "East Asia & Pacific", "Europe & Central Asia", "Europe & Central Asia",
    "Latin America & Caribbean", "Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan",
    "Sub-Saharan Africa", "Sub-Saharan Africa"
  ),
  title = c(
    "East Asia and Pacific; South Asia",
    "Europe and Central Asia (1 of 2)",
    "Europe and Central Asia (2 of 2); no World Bank region",
    "Latin America and the Caribbean; North America",
    "Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan",
    "Sub-Saharan Africa (1 of 2)",
    "Sub-Saharan Africa (2 of 2)"
  )
)

# Every country's place in the annexes: regions in the slides' order, countries alphabetical inside
# a region, and the two long regions cut in half over two slides each
region_order <- c(
  "East Asia & Pacific", "South Asia", "Europe & Central Asia", "Not classified",
  "Latin America & Caribbean", "North America",
  "Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan", "Sub-Saharan Africa"
)
annex_countries <- countries |>
  left_join(short_names, by = "iso3") |>
  mutate(
    region = if_else(wb_region == "not_classified", "Not classified", wb_region),
    inc = unname(INC_CODE[income_group])
  ) |>
  arrange(match(region, region_order), sort_name) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(first_half = row_number() <= ceiling(n() / 2)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    annex_slide = case_when(
      region %in% c("East Asia & Pacific", "South Asia") ~ 1,
      region == "Europe & Central Asia" & first_half ~ 2,
      region %in% c("Europe & Central Asia", "Not classified") ~ 3,
      region %in% c("Latin America & Caribbean", "North America") ~ 4,
      region == "Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan" ~ 5,
      region == "Sub-Saharan Africa" & first_half ~ 6,
      region == "Sub-Saharan Africa" ~ 7
    ),
    annex_position = row_number()
  ) |>
  select(iso3, short, region, inc, annex_slide, annex_position)

# Annex A, one slide: the region line of the slide's lead and the table of every country's latest
# window. We keep this as a function because seven slides use it, each run a second time on the
# report's tables in the final check; `bundle` is `mine` or the report's tables.
annex_a <- function(bundle, slide) {
  this_slide <- annex_slides[annex_slides$slide == slide, ]
  lead_region <- this_slide$lead_region

  # every country on the slide, in the order the slide lists them
  slide_rows <- annex_countries |>
    filter(annex_slide == slide) |>
    left_join(bundle$win, by = "iso3") |>
    arrange(annex_position) |>
    mutate(has_window = !is.na(total))
  table <- slide_rows |>
    transmute(
      Region = unname(REG_LABEL[region]),
      Country = short,
      Inc. = inc,
      `US$` = if_else(has_window, dollars(ghe1, prefix = ""), ""),
      Total = if_else(has_window, signed(total), ""),
      Econ. = if_else(has_window, signed(econ), ""),
      Govt = if_else(has_window, signed(budget), ""),
      Prio. = if_else(has_window, signed(priority), ""),
      Pattern = if_else(
        has_window, paste0(pattern, if_else(lost_priority %in% TRUE, "*", "")), "Not available"
      ),
      Flag = if_else(has_window, coalesce(flag, ""), ""),
      Window = if_else(has_window, paste0(y0, "-", y1), "no constant-price series")
    )

  # the lead: the pattern counts and, for a region with at least eight countries, the median total
  counts <- filter(bundle$pat_reg, key == lead_region)
  latest <- filter(bundle$grp, key == lead_region, period == "W")
  median_text <- ""
  if (grepl("^Carries", latest$status)) {
    median_text <- paste0("; median country ", signed(latest$med_total), " log points a year")
  }
  lead <- paste0(
    REG_LABEL[[lead_region]], ": ", counts$n, " countries, ",
    counts$`Economy-led`, " economy-led, ", counts$`Budget-led`, " budget-led, ",
    counts$`Priority-led`, " priority-led, ", counts$Declining, " declining", median_text
  )

  tables <- list("Lead of the slide" = data.frame(Region = lead))
  tables[[paste0("Annex: ", this_slide$title)]] <- table
  tables
}
```

# Annex B. Every country's prescription for 2029, by World Bank region

Across the seven annex B slides, we give every country's prescription for 2029 on the IMF path, in the same slide sets as annex A:
health's share of government spending (held from the end of the window to 2026); the protect amount, upper ask and
ceiling (P / A / C) in US\$ million at the IMF's 2029 exchange rate and as a real increase in per cent of the 2026 health
budget; the candidate that sets the upper ask; and the years in which the method does not apply. The lead of each slide
gives the region's median protect amount, upper ask and ceiling. "No IMF series" marks a country without IMF projections;
"Not available" in the US\$ column marks a country without an IMF exchange rate for 2029 (Bolivia and Pakistan), whose
real percentages are still available. Each slide gets its own chunk; the slides are tables, so no figure is drawn.

```{r annex-b-helper}
## Annex B: the table of one slide, printing the 2029 prescription row by row.
SET_SHORT <- c(
  "+0.75 a year" = "+0.75", "+0.5 a year" = "+0.5", "+0.25 a year" = "+0.25",
  "Own trend" = "Own trend", "No admissible increase" = "None admissible", "Does not apply" = "-"
)

# Annex B, one slide: the region line of the slide's lead and the table of every
# country's 2029 prescription (IMF path). A function for the same reason as annex_a();
# `bundle` is `mine` or the report's tables.
annex_b <- function(bundle, slide) {
  this_slide <- annex_slides[annex_slides$slide == slide, ]
  imf_path <- filter(bundle$rx, variant == "imf")

  # the years from 2027 to 2029 in which the method does not apply
  years_not_applying <- imf_path |>
    filter(has_data %in% TRUE, !(applies %in% TRUE)) |>
    arrange(year) |>
    group_by(iso3) |>
    summarise(not_apply = paste(year, collapse = ", "))

  # Every country on the slide with its 2029 row. A country without a GHED base (Cuba) has no row
  # and is listed with nothing computed. Amounts are in US$ million, and the real rise in % of the
  # 2026 health budget, for the protect amount, the upper ask and the ceiling (P / A / C).
  slide_rows <- annex_countries |>
    filter(annex_slide == slide) |>
    left_join(filter(imf_path, year == 2029), by = "iso3") |>
    left_join(years_not_applying, by = "iso3") |>
    arrange(annex_position) |>
    mutate(
      has_base = !is.na(variant),
      with_data = has_data %in% TRUE,
      usd_protect = coalesce(dollars(d_protect_usd / 1e6, prefix = ""), "-"),
      usd_ask = coalesce(dollars(ask_usd / 1e6, prefix = ""), "-"),
      usd_ceiling = coalesce(dollars(d_all_usd / 1e6, prefix = ""), "-"),
      pct_protect = coalesce(scales::comma(d_protect_pct, accuracy = 1), "-"),
      pct_ask = coalesce(scales::comma(ask_pct, accuracy = 1), "-"),
      pct_ceiling = coalesce(scales::comma(d_all_pct, accuracy = 1), "-")
    )
  table <- slide_rows |>
    transmute(
      Region = unname(REG_LABEL[region]),
      Country = short,
      Inc. = inc,
      `Share %` = if_else(has_base, one_decimal(h), ""),
      `US$ million P / A / C` = case_when(
        !has_base ~ "No GHED base",
        !with_data ~ "No IMF series",
        is.na(d_protect_usd) ~ "Not available",
        .default = paste(usd_protect, usd_ask, usd_ceiling, sep = " / ")
      ),
      `Real % P / A / C` = if_else(
        with_data, paste(pct_protect, pct_ask, pct_ceiling, sep = " / "), ""
      ),
      `Ask set by` = if_else(with_data, unname(SET_SHORT[setter_label]), ""),
      `Does not apply` = if_else(with_data, coalesce(not_apply, "-"), "")
    )

  # the lead: the region's median protect amount, upper ask and ceiling
  medians <- filter(bundle$rx_grp, key == this_slide$lead_region, variant == "imf", year == 2029)
  lead <- paste0(
    REG_LABEL[[this_slide$lead_region]], ", median of ", medians$n,
    ": protect ", share_pct(medians$med_d_protect_pct),
    ", upper ask ", share_pct(medians$med_ask_pct),
    ", ceiling ", whole_pct(medians$med_d_all_pct), " of the 2026 health budget, real"
  )

  tables <- list("Lead of the slide" = data.frame(Region = lead))
  tables[[paste0("Annex: ", this_slide$title)]] <- table
  tables
}
```

# Check against the report's outputs

In the final chunk, we run every slide chunk a second time, now on the report's own output tables (the tables the deck was
built from), and compare the two results cell by cell as each cell would be printed, to the printed decimal. The table counts
the numbers compared on each slide (every number inside a cell, including years and counts) and the cells of text, such
as country names and pattern labels. Any mismatch stops the render with an error and lists the cells that differ.

```{r check-against-report, results = "asis"}
## Final check: every number the slides print, computed in this file, against the same
## number recomputed from the report's output tables (data/reference_outputs.rds).
## Stops with an error on any mismatch.
reference <- readRDS("data/reference_outputs.rds")
stopifnot(all(REF_NAMES %in% names(reference)))
report_tables <- reference[REF_NAMES]
names(report_tables) <- names(REF_NAMES) # the same names as in `mine`

# We read the code of the 34 slide chunks from this file: from the Rmd being knitted, or from the
# file in this folder when the chunks are run one by one in RStudio
rmd_file <- knitr::current_input()
if (is.null(rmd_file)) rmd_file <- "global-decomposition-deck.Rmd"
rmd_lines <- readLines(rmd_file, encoding = "UTF-8")
chunk_starts <- grep("^```\\{r slide-[0-9]+", rmd_lines)
chunk_ends <- grep("^```\\s*$", rmd_lines)
stopifnot(length(chunk_starts) == 34)

# all the cells of a slide's tables, as they are printed, table by table and column by column
cells <- function(tables) {
  printed <- character(0)
  for (table in tables) {
    for (column in table) printed <- c(printed, as.character(column))
  }
  printed
}

# We run each slide chunk twice more, each time in an environment of its own: once on this
# file's tables, and once with `mine` replaced by the report's tables. A run leaves the
# slide's tables in `tables`; capture.output() drops what the run prints, and invisible()
# keeps its figure from being drawn again.
result <- NULL
details <- list()
for (start in chunk_starts) {
  slide_id <- sub("^```\\{r (slide-[0-9]+).*$", "\\1", rmd_lines[start])
  end <- min(chunk_ends[chunk_ends > start])
  slide_code <- parse(text = rmd_lines[(start + 1):(end - 1)])
  this_run <- new.env()
  report_run <- new.env()
  report_run$mine <- report_tables
  capture.output(invisible(eval(slide_code, this_run)))
  capture.output(invisible(eval(slide_code, report_run)))

  # a cell differs if only one side is missing, or if both are there and differ
  ours <- cells(this_run$tables)
  theirs <- cells(report_run$tables)
  if (length(ours) != length(theirs)) {
    differ <- seq_along(ours)
  } else {
    missing_differs <- is.na(ours) != is.na(theirs)
    value_differs <- !is.na(ours) & !is.na(theirs) & ours != theirs
    differ <- which(missing_differs | value_differs)
  }
  if (length(differ) > 0) {
    details[[slide_id]] <- data.frame(
      slide = slide_id,
      this_file = ours[differ],
      report = theirs[differ][seq_along(differ)]
    )
  }

  # every number inside a cell counts, including years and counts
  numbers_in_cells <- regmatches(ours, gregexpr("[0-9][0-9,]*(\\.[0-9]+)?", ours))
  result <- rbind(result, data.frame(
    Slide = sub("slide-", "Slide ", slide_id),
    `Numbers compared` = sum(lengths(numbers_in_cells)),
    `Text cells compared` = sum(!grepl("[0-9]", ours)),
    Mismatches = length(differ),
    Result = if (length(differ) > 0) "FAIL" else "pass",
    check.names = FALSE
  ))
}
all_slides <- data.frame(
  Slide = "All slides",
  `Numbers compared` = sum(result$`Numbers compared`),
  `Text cells compared` = sum(result$`Text cells compared`),
  Mismatches = sum(result$Mismatches),
  Result = if (all(result$Result == "pass")) "pass" else "FAIL",
  check.names = FALSE
)
result <- rbind(result, all_slides)
cat("\n\n")
print(knitr::kable(
  result,
  caption = "Printed numbers: this file against the report's outputs", align = "lrrrl"
))
cat("\n\n")
if (length(details) > 0) {
  differences <- bind_rows(details)
  print(knitr::kable(differences, caption = "Cells that differ"))
  stop(
    "The numbers printed by this file differ from the report's outputs on ", length(details),
    " slide(s)."
  )
}
```
